2026年上海外滩旅游指南：最佳景点、步行路线、夜景及旅行贴士 
计划第一次去上海外滩游览？
这份完整的《上海外滩指南》涵盖了您在游览前需要了解的一切，包括 1.5 公里的外滩滨水区、著名历史建筑、最佳步行路线、黄浦江游船、南京东路站、附近的景点（如豫园、上海中心大厦和东方明珠电视塔），以及最佳游览时间、摄影技巧和实用旅行建议，帮助您探索上海最具标志性的地标之一。 
 外滩必看亮点 
 历史建筑、和平饭店、海关大楼、外滩公牛和黄浦公园 
 最佳步行体验 
 1.5公里外滩、南京东路、外白渡桥及夜景 
 天际线和河流景色 
 上海中心大厦、东方明珠、黄浦江游船和现代摩天大楼 
 完美的 
 首次来上海的游客、摄影爱好者、家庭游客及私人上海旅游 
外滩概览 
 信息速览信息
 地点上海市中心中山东一路
 长度1.5公里长的海滨长廊
 最佳访问时间清晨、日落前或夜幕降临后
 建议参观时间2–4 小时
 最近的地铁南京东路站，地铁2号线和10号线
 入学咨询免费
 水上巡航30 分钟至 3.5 小时
 附近景点豫园、南京路、上海中心大厦和东方明珠电视塔
外滩值得一游吗？ 
当然。如果您是第一次来上海，外滩绝对应该列入您的行程清单之首。
外滩沿黄浦江绵延1.5公里，是上海最著名的滨水区，也是中国最具代表性的地标之一。它巧妙地融合了昔日公共租界52余座历史建筑与江对岸上海中心大厦、东方明珠电视塔及其他现代摩天大楼的未来主义天际线，形成鲜明对比。
无论您是对历史、建筑、摄影、当地文化感兴趣，还是仅仅想欣赏世界一流的城市天际线，外滩都能为您带来难忘的体验——而且完全免费参观。 
为什么要去外滩？ 
沿着上海标志性的1.5公里滨水长廊漫步。
欣赏哥特式、巴洛克式、装饰艺术式和新古典主义风格的历史建筑。
隔着黄浦江，饱览浦东现代化天际线的全景。
参观和平饭店、海关大楼、外滩牛、黄浦公园等著名地标。
乘坐黄浦江游船，从不同的角度欣赏这座城市。
探索附近的景点，包括豫园、南京路、上海中心大厦和东方明珠电视塔。
在黄浦公园观看当地居民练习太极拳和晨练。
体验上海最壮观的日落和夜景之一。 
外滩必游景点 
漫步上海外滩，就像探索一座露天建筑博物馆。短短1.5公里的路程，您将途经宏伟的殖民时期地标建筑、著名酒店、历史悠久的金融大厦、宁静的江畔公园，以及一些俯瞰浦东现代天际线的最佳观景点。 
和平饭店 
和平饭店是外滩最知名的地标之一。这座装饰艺术风格的杰作于1929年开业，以其绿色的铜屋顶、优雅的外立面以及与老上海的悠久渊源而闻名。
即使您不住在这里，也值得从外面看看或者进去欣赏一下大堂。
亮点：装饰艺术风格建筑、历史悠久的豪华酒店、绿色金字塔屋顶、外滩景观。 
海关 
海关大楼毗邻和平饭店，是外滩的另一标志性建筑。它于1927年竣工，其钟楼近百年来一直俯瞰着黄浦江。
钟楼仍然是中山东路沿线最具标志性的建筑之一。
亮点：标志性钟楼、新古典主义建筑、热门拍照地点。 
前汇丰银行大厦 
香港上海汇丰银行大厦曾是远东地区最令人印象深刻的银行大楼之一。其宏伟的穹顶、古典的柱式以及金融历史反映了上海在20世纪初作为主要银行中心的地位。
亮点：历史悠久的金融地标、古典建筑、上海银行业历史。 
德意志银行 
外滩铜牛象征着上海的金融信心，常被拿来与纽约华尔街铜牛相提并论。它是外滩沿岸一个热门的拍照打卡点，虽然停留时间不长。
亮点：金融象征、旅游拍照点、海滨长廊上的便捷休憩站。 
黄浦公园 
外滩北端的黄浦公园是远离喧嚣的静谧之所。清晨，您经常可以看到当地居民练习太极拳、跳舞、慢跑或进行晨练。
亮点：当地文化、晨练太极、河景、休闲绿地。 
外白渡桥 
外白渡桥，又称花园桥，连接外滩和苏州河，是上海最著名的历史桥梁之一，也是摄影爱好者的热门地点。
从这里，您可以同时欣赏到外滩的历史建筑、苏州河和浦东的现代天际线。
亮点：历史悠久的钢桥、天际线景观、日落摄影。 
外滩最佳步行路线 
游览上海外滩的最佳方式是步行。主要步行街长约1.5公里，您可以悠闲地漫步其中。
这条路线可以在 2 到 3 小时内完成，包括拍照和短暂休息的时间。 
 Stop 停止推荐时间
 南京东路站10分钟
 和平饭店10-15 分钟
 海关大楼及原汇丰银行大楼15-20 分钟
 外滩海滨长廊20-30 分钟
 德意志银行5-10 分钟
 黄浦公园20分钟
 外白渡桥20-30 分钟
建议路线 
从上海地铁2号线或10号线南京东路站出发。沿着上海最繁忙的街道之一南京路向东走，直到到达外滩。
从那里继续沿着滨海大道前行，途经和平饭店、海关大楼、原汇丰银行大厦和外滩牛。然后步行前往黄浦公园，最后到达外白渡桥，欣赏苏州河和浦东天际线的经典景色。 
当地小费 
请在日落前60-90分钟开始您的步行之旅。您将有机会欣赏白日里的外滩，感受黄浦江上绚丽的日落景色，并留下来欣赏上海著名的夜景。 
外滩最佳拍照地点 
无论你使用智能手机还是专业相机，外滩都是上海最佳的摄影地点之一。 
外滩海滨长廊 
这里是拍摄上海天际线、黄浦江、东方明珠电视塔和上海中心大厦的经典地点。
最适合拍摄：城市天际线、日落、夜景、广角照片。 
外白渡桥 
外白渡桥是捕捉老上海与现代浦东风情的绝佳取景地，尤其在日落和夜幕降临时分，景色更是美不胜收。
最适合：桥梁摄影、苏州河摄影、长时间曝光夜景摄影。 
黄浦公园 
清晨来访，可以看到当地人的生活景象，包括太极拳、慢跑和在河边晨练。
最适合：体验当地文化、欣赏晨光、拍摄安静的照片。 
和平酒店外 
费尔蒙和平酒店是建筑摄影的最佳地点之一，尤其是在早上人比较少的时候。
最适合：装饰艺术细节、历史建筑、街头摄影。 
德意志银行 
外滩牛是一处简单却很受欢迎的地标性拍照景点，尤其是在浦东天际线的映衬下，更是如此。
最适合：旅行人像和地标照片。 
摄影技巧 
清晨前往，人会少一些。
为了获得最佳光线，请在日落前到达。
天黑后留下来，可以拍摄灯光璀璨的城市天际线照片。
使用广角镜头拍摄城市天际线。
高峰时段请勿用三脚架阻挡海滨长廊。 
游览外滩的最佳时间 
外滩全天开放，但游览体验会因时间不同而有所变化。 
清晨
清晨最适合悠闲漫步，感受当地文化，而且人也比较少。您或许会在黄浦公园看到当地居民练习太极拳或进行晨练。
下午
下午是欣赏外滩历史建筑的好时机，包括和平饭店、海关大楼和原汇丰银行大厦。夏季，外滩天气炎热潮湿。
日落之前
这是最佳游览时间。建议在日落前一小时左右到达，这样可以欣赏到白天的景色、日落的色彩以及夜晚的灯光秀。
夜晚
夜幕降临，外滩摇身一变，成为上海最壮观的景点之一。历史建筑灯火辉煌，而江对岸的上海中心大厦、东方明珠电视塔和现代摩天大楼则构成了一幅令人叹为观止的天际线。 
最佳季节 
 季节天气推荐
 春季12–22°C步行舒适
 Summer27–34°C天气炎热潮湿，晚上最舒服
 秋季18–26°C天空晴朗，天气宜人。
 冬季2–12°C人少景美
总体而言，春季和秋季是最舒适的季节，但一年四季都值得在晚上来此游览。 
黄浦江游船之旅：值得吗？ 
黄浦江游船是体验外滩和上海天际线的最佳方式之一。沿着江边漫步可以近距离欣赏历史建筑，而乘船游览则可以从水上欣赏黄浦江两岸的景色。 
您会看到什么？ 
游轮航行期间，您可以看到：
外滩历史悠久的滨水区
上海塔
东方明珠电视塔
上海环球金融中心
金茂大厦
陆家嘴金融区
黄浦江夜景 
巡航时间 
 邮轮类型修读年限最适合
 短途观光游轮30-50 分钟初次来访者
 标准游轮60-90 分钟家庭和情侣
 晚餐巡航2–3.5 小时晚间用餐及美景
对于大多数旅行者来说，45 到 60 分钟的观光游船就足够了。 
最佳邮轮旅行时间 
夜间游船最受欢迎，因为可以欣赏到灯火辉煌的外滩和浦东天际线。如果您想要更安静的体验，可以选择白天的游船。 
这值得么？ 
是的，尤其对于初次来上海的游客来说。乘船游览上海能让你更全面地欣赏这座城市的风光，而且在漫步外滩之后，乘船游览更是锦上添花。 
同一天可以游览的附近景点 
外滩的一大优势在于其优越的地理位置。上海众多著名景点都近在咫尺。 
南京路 
南京路是上海最著名的购物街，与外滩自然相连。许多游客从南京东路站步行前往外滩。
行程时间：步行约10分钟。 
豫园 
豫园是上海最著名的古典园林之一，园内亭台楼阁、假山石林、池塘碧波荡漾，建筑风格古朴典雅。周边老城区也是品尝小吃、购买纪念品的热门去处。
行程时间：乘坐出租车或地铁约10分钟。 
上海塔 
上海中心大厦高632米，是中国最高的建筑。其观景台可俯瞰外滩、黄浦江和上海市中心全景。
行程时间：乘坐地铁约需 10-15 分钟。 
东方明珠电视塔 
东方明珠电视塔是上海最知名的地标之一，它隔江与外滩遥遥相望。
很容易将它与外滩游览结合起来，特别是如果您乘坐渡轮、地铁或外滩观光隧道前往浦东的话。 
外滩观光隧道 
外滩观光隧道连接外滩和浦东，位于黄浦江下。它更像是一种旅游体验而非实用的交通方式，但或许能给家庭游客带来乐趣。 
跨河渡轮 
乘坐公共渡轮是横渡黄浦江最便宜、最具当地特色的方式之一。只需支付少量费用，就能欣赏到壮丽的城市天际线。 
半日游和全日游行程示例 
半日外滩行程 
 时间租赁计划
 3:30左右返回码头抵达南京东路站
 4:00左右返回码头步行前往外滩
 4:30左右返回码头参观和平饭店、海关大楼和外滩公牛。
 5:30左右返回码头步行即可到达黄埔公园和外白渡桥
 6:30左右返回码头欣赏日落和夜景
 7:30左右返回码头在外滩附近享用晚餐或在屋顶酒吧小酌一杯。
上海一日游行程 
 时间租赁计划
 中午 9:00 点游览豫园和古城
 中午 11:30 点在豫园或南京路附近吃午饭
 1:00左右返回码头探索南京路
 3:30左右返回码头步行前往外滩
 5:00左右返回码头游览黄浦公园和外白渡桥
 6:30左右返回码头欣赏外滩夜景
 8:00左右返回码头乘坐黄浦江游船
外滩的历史与建筑 
外滩的历史始于19世纪中叶，当时上海在第一次鸦片战争后对外开放。英国租界沿着黄浦江西岸发展起来，该地区逐渐成为上海的商业和金融中心。
20世纪初，各大银行、贸易公司、航运公司和外国机构纷纷在今天的中山东路沿线设立总部。由于其在国际金融和对外贸易中的重要性，该地区被称为“东方华尔街”。
如今，外滩常被誉为一座活生生的建筑博物馆。这里历史建筑林立，风格多样，包括哥特式、巴洛克式、新古典主义、文艺复兴复兴式和装饰艺术风格。和平饭店、海关大楼和汇丰银行大厦等地标性建筑，无不体现着老上海的财富与雄心。
如今外滩之所以如此引人注目，在于它与江对岸的鲜明对比。一边是上海殖民时代的建筑，另一边则是浦东的现代摩天大楼，包括上海中心大厦和东方明珠电视塔。在中国，很少有地方能像这片滨江地区一样，如此清晰地展现出国家的变迁。 
如何前往外滩 
外滩是上海市中心最容易到达的景点之一。 
乘地铁
乘坐上海地铁2号线或10号线到南京东路站。从该站步行约10分钟即可到达外滩。
乘坐出租车或滴滴
目的地可以选择外滩或中山东一路。出租车和滴滴出行都很方便，但周末、节假日和晚间交通可能会比较拥堵。
坐巴士
33路、55路、65路和135路公交车在外滩附近设有站点。
渡轮
您可以乘坐公共渡轮横渡黄浦江，往返于外滩和浦东之间。价格便宜，充满当地风情，而且风景优美。 
 交通信息
 地铁地铁2号线和10号线至南京东路站
 步行距离车站约10分钟路程
 出租车/滴滴交通拥堵时虽然方便但速度较慢。
 公共汽车33号、55号、65号和135号公路
 轮渡过黄浦江到浦东
外滩附近有哪些餐厅？ 
外滩周边地区应有尽有，从上海当地小吃到可以欣赏城市天际线的屋顶餐厅，一应俱全。 
小笼包 
想体验地道美食，不妨尝尝上海著名的汤包——小笼包。豫园、南京路附近以及周边餐馆都能找到不错的选择。 
屋顶餐厅和酒吧 
想要欣赏城市天际线美景，可以选择外滩附近的屋顶餐厅或酒吧。“The Fellas”餐厅是欣赏黄浦江夜景、品尝饮品和享用晚餐的热门之选。 
外滩3号、5号和6号 
外滩三号、五号和六号等历史建筑如今已改建为餐厅、咖啡馆和酒吧。如果您想在用餐的同时感受建筑氛围，这些都是不错的选择。
最佳建议：为了欣赏最佳日落景色，请在日落前 30-60 分钟预订餐桌。 
实用旅行小贴士 
如果想同时欣赏白天和夜晚的景色，请在日落前前往。
清晨前往，人少，还能欣赏当地的太极拳表演。
高峰时段请乘坐地铁，因为交通可能会比较拥堵。
请穿着舒适的鞋子漫步外滩及周边街道。
天黑后留下来欣赏城市天际线的灯光。
将外滩与豫园、南京路、上海中心大厦或东方明珠电视塔结合起来游览。
如果你不喜欢人多的地方，就避开中国的主要节假日。
查看天气预报，尤其是在夏季，上海天气炎热潮湿。
请携带电量充足的相机或手机，以便拍摄夜间照片。
如果想以低廉的价格欣赏过河景色，可以试试乘坐公共渡轮。

如果您想在知识渊博的当地导游的带领下探索外滩、豫园、上海中心大厦、南京路以及上海的隐秘街区，GoChinaQuest 可以帮助您打造符合您节奏和兴趣的私人上海之旅。

常見問題解答 
 外滩可以免费参观吗？ 
是的。沿着外滩漫步完全免费。但黄浦江游船、观景台、餐厅和外滩观光隧道等自选项目需要单独购票。 
 什么时候是游览外滩的最佳时间？ 
最佳时间是日落前一小时左右。这样您既能欣赏到白天的景色，又能欣赏到黄浦江上的日落美景，还能看到上海灯火通明后壮丽的天际线。 
 离外滩最近的地铁站是哪个？ 
距离外滩最近的车站是上海地铁2号线和10号线的南京东路站。从那里步行大约10分钟即可到达外滩。 
 我在外滩应该待多久？ 
大多数游客会花 2 到 4 个小时游览海滨，拍摄城市天际线，参观历史建筑，并享受附近的景点。 
 黄浦江游轮之旅值得吗？ 
是的。黄浦江游船之旅能让您从完全不同的视角欣赏上海，既能饱览历史悠久的外滩风光，又能从江面上欣赏浦东的现代天际线。 
 外滩附近有哪些景点可以游览？ 
附近的热门景点包括南京路、豫园、上海中心大厦、东方明珠电视塔、黄浦公园和外滩观光隧道。许多游客会选择一天内游览其中几个景点。

title: The Bund, Shanghai: Maps, How to Visit, and What to See
text:
Home
 Destinations
 Shanghai 
The Bund, Shanghai: Maps, How to Visit, and What to See
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated Aug. 31, 2026 
The Bund is Shanghai's most iconic landmark, and if it's your first visit, give yourself 2–3 hours if you want both the historic buildings and the skyline; 30–60 minutes is enough for a quick photo stop.
For the classic night scene, arrive before sunset and watch the city lights come on gradually, enjoying the sharp contrast between day and night. 
If you value open space and a calmer pace over close-up detail, the North Bund offers a quieter skyline view, but you'll miss some of the intimate Bund atmosphere.
Main Bund or North Bund: Which One Should You Choose?
The Main Bund and the North Bund offer two very different ways to experience Shanghai's waterfront.
For most first-time visitors, we recommend the Main Bund.
The Main Bund is the famous stretch along Zhongshan East 1st Road, where you walk beside Shanghai's historic waterfront buildings — the architectural collection often referred to as the "Museum of World Architecture." Across the Huangpu River is the Pudong skyline.
The North Bund sits further north, around the Huangpu River and Suzhou Creek. It gives you more space, fewer people, and wider views back toward both Pudong and the historic Bund.
So the choice is simple:
Choose the Main Bund if you want to get close to Shanghai's historic buildings and understand the stories behind them.
Choose the North Bund if photography, open space, and skyline views matter more to you than architectural history.
5-Day Shanghai, Hangzhou and Suzhou Explore the Elegant China
Main Bund Cultural Walk: Our Top Choice for First-Time Visitors
The Bund
Time needed: 2–3 hours
Best for: First-time visitors, history and architecture lovers, families, and couples
If this is your first time in Shanghai, this is the route we recommend.
The Main Bund is not just about standing by the river and taking the classic skyline photo. The real experience is in the buildings behind you.
Along this stretch are Shanghai's famous historic waterfront buildings, built in dramatically different architectural styles. But unless you know what you are looking at, it is easy to walk past them without understanding why they matter.
Our route: Former Astor House area → Garden Bridge → Peace Hotel → former HSBC Building → Bund waterfront
On our private walking tour, we don't just point at the buildings from the street. Depending on opening hours and access arrangements, we can take you inside selected historic buildings and explain the stories behind them.
You will see how this part of Shanghai developed during the 1920s and 1930s, when the city became one of Asia's most international trading centers, and how foreign banks, hotels, and trading companies shaped the architecture that still defines the Bund today.
At the same time, you still get the classic view across the Huangpu River toward Pudong's modern skyline.
This is the best route if you want to understand why the Bund is important, rather than simply take a photo of it. And that is how we design the rest of our Shanghai tours too — not simply taking you to see the city, but helping you experience it and understand the stories behind it.
9-Day Beijing ,Xian and Shanghai Tour China Family Classic Tour 
North Bund Walk: Better for Space and Photography
Shanghai North Bund with Little Egg
Time needed: 1.5–2 hours
Best for: Photographers, repeat visitors, and travelers who prefer fewer crowds
The North Bund is where we would send you if you have already seen the Main Bund — or if you care more about photography than getting close to the historic buildings.
The waterfront here is more open, with fewer crowds and more room to walk.
You also get several different angles for photographing the Pudong skyline, the historic Bund buildings, and the Huangpu River. Instead of walking directly among the historic architecture, you are looking back toward it from a greater distance.
That makes the North Bund a better choice if your priority is wide skyline shots rather than architectural details and historical stories.
It can also be a smart alternative during extremely busy travel periods, such as the Labour Day holiday or National Day Golden Week, when the Main Bund can become particularly crowded.
Our route: Shanghai Postal Museum → Garden Bridge → North Bund waterfront → Little Egg → riverside viewpoints
This is a looser walk built around viewpoints rather than a historical narrative. You can stop where the views interest you rather than following a strict sightseeing sequence.
However, for most first-time visitors, we still would not choose the North Bund instead of the Main Bund.
You may get more space and more photo opportunities, but you lose the chance to walk directly among the buildings that made the Bund famous.
5-Day Shanghai and Hangzhou High Tech Tour 
When Is the Best Time to Visit the Bund?
Arrive Around 2 PM: Get the Full Bund Experience (Most Recommended)
In-depth tour of the Bund in Shanghai
This is our top recommendation if you are visiting the Bund for the first time.
This gives you enough daylight to see the historic buildings properly, rather than viewing them only as illuminated facades at night. You can spend around 2.5 hours on an in-depth walk, then take a break for afternoon tea before returning to the waterfront as the sky begins to change.
By staying until after sunset, you get both sides of the Bund in one visit: the architectural details and stories that are easiest to appreciate during the day, followed by the Pudong skyline as the lights gradually come on.
Arrive 30–60 Minutes Before Sunset: Best for the Skyline Night View
Watching the sunset on the Bund in Shanghai
If the Pudong skyline is all you really want to see, there is no need to spend the entire afternoon at the Bund.
Arrive around 30–60 minutes before sunset and stay until the city lights are fully on.
The advantage is not just seeing Shanghai at night. You get to watch the scene change from daylight to dusk, then to a fully illuminated skyline. This transition is what creates the dramatic contrast behind many of the Bund's most recognizable views.
As a rough guide, sunset is usually around 6:30–7:00 PM in summer and 5:00–5:30 PM in winter, although the exact time changes throughout the year.
If you arrive only after dark, the view is still impressive — but you will miss the transition.
Go Around 8:30 AM on a Weekday: Best for Avoiding Crowds
On a weekday morning, the Bund in Shanghai is sparsely populated.
Around 8:30 AM on a weekday, traffic is light, the promenade is nearly empty, and you can walk or jog along the river with almost no one around.
However, most historic buildings won't be open yet, so you may need to wait half an hour to an hour before embarking cultural walking tour, or you want the exterior views and a quiet atmosphere.
8-Day Shanghai, Hangzhou, Suzhou Family TourShanghai-Hangzhou-Wuzhen-Suzhou 
FAQs About the Bund
Do I Need to Take a Huangpu River Cruise?
Huangpu River cruise at night for the Bund
Time needed: about 45–60 minutes
Best time: 7 PM departures, when the lights start on, and the atmosphere is at its best
Best for: Families, couples, photographers, and visitors who want the skyline without walking the entire waterfront
We recommend taking a Huangpu River cruise at night.
The Bund promenade gives you the classic view toward Pudong, but from the river, you can see both sides of Shanghai at once.
On one side are the historic buildings of the Bund. On the other is Pudong's modern skyline.
Seeing the two riverbanks from the water gives you a much clearer sense of the contrast that defines Shanghai: its colonial-era architecture facing one of the world's most futuristic skylines.
It is also a much more relaxed way to experience the waterfront. Instead of competing for space on a crowded promenade or walking the entire length of the Bund, you can simply sit back and watch the skyline unfold around you.
Our preferred option is the classic route departing from Shiliupu Marina, which takes you past many of Shanghai's most recognizable waterfront landmarks.
Tips
If it is raining heavily, foggy, or visibility is poor, we would reconsider.
The main reason to take the cruise is the view, and if the skyline is hidden by mist or low clouds, much of the experience is lost.
Is the Bund Free?
Yes. The Main Bund waterfront promenade is free.
You do not need a ticket to walk beside the river or photograph the historic buildings from outside.
Several museums and public interiors are also free, including the China Securities Museum and Shanghai Postal Museum, subject to their opening hours and admission arrangements.
However, a Huangpu River cruise requires payment, and the price depends on the pier, boat, route, and ticket type.
So if your budget is tight, you can only experience the Bund without paying for a cruise.

title: Jade Buddha Temple, Shanghai: What to See and How to Visit
text:
Home
 Destinations
 Shanghai 
Jade Buddha Temple, Shanghai: What to See and How to Visit
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated Sep. 24, 2026 
Jade Buddha Temple was built around 1918 in the style of the Song Dynasty (960-1279). Named for its 1.9-meter-high white jade Buddha, Jade Buddha Temple is worth about 1–1.5 hours if you want to see the temple's most prized treasure and experience an active Buddhist temple.
If you are on a tight schedule, or your priority is the Bund, Shanghai's old neighborhoods, or the city's modern skyline, you can skip it.
Visit it if you want:
to see Shanghai's famous jade Buddhas;
to experience an active Buddhist temple;
to learn more about Chinese Buddhist culture;
or to spend some time with traditional temple architecture.
Skip it if you want:
Shanghai's skyline and modern cityscape;
old neighborhoods and cafés;
or a very short list of the city's highest-priority sights.
What to See Inside Jade Buddha Temple
Jade Buddha Temple
Address: 170 Anyuan Road, Putuo District, Shanghai
Opening hours: 8:00–16:30 on regular days
Admission: Free
Metro: Line 13, Jiangning Road Station, Exit 3
Walk from the station: About 5 minutes
Recommended visit: 1–1.5 hours
1. The Two Jade Buddhas: The Absolute Must-see
The white jade Buddha of Jade Buddha Temple
The temple is named after two white jade Buddhas brought to Shanghai from Myanmar in the late 19th century.
The most important stop is the Jade Buddha Hall, where you can see the seated jade Buddha, about 1.9 meters high. Then continue to the Reclining Buddha Hall to see the smaller reclining jade Buddha, which represents the Buddha before entering nirvana.
If you only have one hour, prioritize these two halls. You don't need to inspect every hall or Buddhist statue to understand why the temple is significant.
2. Traditional Chinese Temple Architecture
Roof decorations of the Jade Buddha Temple
The jade Buddhas are the main attraction, but the temple itself is also worth noticing.
As you walk through the complex, look for the symmetrical layout, yellow walls, traditional rooflines, courtyards, and carved decorative details.
The architecture gives you a very different side of Shanghai from the skyscrapers around the Bund and Lujiazui.
If you enjoy Chinese architecture, allow a little extra time to walk rather than rushing directly from one Buddha hall to the next.
Photography Tips
If you want photos, focus on the architecture, courtyards, roof details, and overall temple atmosphere rather than trying to photograph every hall.
Photography is restricted in certain worship areas or during religious activities. Follow the signs inside the temple.
3. Taste the Vegetarian Cuisine
The temple also has a vegetarian food section serving traditional Buddhist vegetarian dishes with Shanghai-style cooking (priced at 50–70 RMB per person).
This works well for vegans, or if you want to eat immediately after visiting rather than finding another restaurant.
I would treat the vegetarian food as an optional add-on, not the main reason to visit. Come for the jade Buddhas first.
Check detailed information on its official website: Jade Buddha Temple.
5-Day Shanghai, Hangzhou and Suzhou Explore the Elegant China
How Much Time Do You Need at Jade Buddha Temple?
Koi Pond at the Jade Buddha Temple
Less than 1 hour: See the two jade Buddhas, look around the main halls, and leave.
1–2 hours: See the two Buddhas, explore the main architectural spaces, and spend some time observing the temple atmosphere. This is the amount of time we would suggest for most travelers.
2–3 hours: Worth considering if you have a strong interest in Buddhism, Chinese temple architecture, religious culture, or an interest in having a vegan meal inside.
If you are visiting Shanghai for only one or two days and Buddhist culture is not a priority, don't force Jade Buddha Temple into your itinerary simply because it is famous.
The time may be better spent on the Bund, the Former French Concession, or another experience that matches your interests more closely.
If you're unsure whether it deserves a place in your short Shanghai itinerary, tell us how many days you have and what else you want to see. We can help you decide where it fits without adding unnecessary cross-city travel.
8-Day Beijing–Xi'an–Shanghai Tour China Golden Triangle
Jade Buddha Temple vs. Jing'an Temple: Which Fits Your Itinerary?
Shanghai Jing'an Temple night view
 Jade Buddha Temple
 Jing'an Temple
 Main appeal
 Jade Buddhas and Buddhist culture
 Temple architecture + modern Shanghai
 Experience
 Slower and more cultural
 Quicker and more visual
 Suggested time
 1–2 hours
 About 30–60 minutes for a quick photo
 Best for
 Travelers interested in Buddhism and traditional temple culture
 Travelers who want a temple stop without spending much time
Choose Jing'an Temple for a quick architectural stop, while opting for Jade Buddha Temple if you want to spend more time understanding Buddhist culture and seeing the famous jade Buddhas.
You don't need to visit both unless temples are a specific interest.
5-Day Shanghai and Hangzhou High Tech Tour 
How to Fit Jade Buddha Temple into Your Shanghai Itinerary
Jade Buddha Temple works best as one stop within a Former French Concession route, rather than as a destination that requires a special trip across Shanghai.
For example, you could visit the Former French Concession in the morning, have lunch nearby, and then continue to Jade Buddha Temple for a cultural immersion.
If your Shanghai itinerary is already full, don't add the temple just to collect another famous attraction.
If you want to visit Jade Buddha Temple without wasting time crossing Shanghai, we can build it into your private sightseeing route and combine it with nearby experiences that match your interests.

title: Best/Worst Times to Visit Shanghai 2026: Tips for All Months
text:
Home
 Destinations
 Shanghai 
Best/Worst Times to Visit Shanghai 2026: Tips for All Months
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated Apr. 13, 2026 
We're often asked when the best time is to visit Shanghai.
Shanghai has a humid subtropical climate with four distinct seasons, and there's something to enjoy anytime you visit.
The simplest answer: autumn (September to November) is sunny, mild, and dry, and relatively uncrowded. Spring (March to May) is also lovely, though a bit more humid with occasional light rain.
But if you want to avoid the crowds or catch a specific seasonal highlight, a general "best season" answer isn't always enough.
Based on our experience and customer feedback, we've found that timing your trip around specific periods can make a big difference. We'll share those insights below, so you can plan a vacation that's as close to perfect as possible.
Considering your stay in Shanghai may not be too long, you may also want to know how to plan a Shanghai trip that meets your needs and travel length.
Content Preview
Autumn and Spring: Top Choices
Winter: The Cheapest Time
Summer: The Worst Time Without Strategies
Dates to Avoid in 2026/2027
Autumn and Spring: Your Top Choices
Wukang Mansion in Autumn, Shanghai, China
Autumn (September to November) is the best season to travel to Shanghai. 
Summer crowds, the rainy season, and heatwaves begin to fade, prices return to normal, and the weather is perfect for leisurely city walks.
For more stable weather, plan your trip for later than mid-September, and check the forecast before you go. Typhoons can affect Shanghai from July to September, but the probability drops sharply after mid-September.
Beyond weather, if you're hoping to see Shanghai's autumn colors, aim for mid-November to mid-December. Due to global warming, this cooler window has become a more reliable time for foliage.

Cherry blossoms in full bloom at Guyi Garden in Shanghai in spring
Spring (March to May) is also a great time to visit Shanghai, offering pleasant days around 15°C (59°F) but more light rains (9 rainy days vs. 6 rainy days) compared to autumn.
If you want to experience the traditional Chinese ink painting-like beauty of the water towns, March and April are the best months to visit.
Early to mid-March can be relatively cold, so if you're sensitive to the cold, consider visiting after mid-March.
Late March to early April is the cherry blossom season, where you can enjoy great scenery at spots like Hongkou Football Stadium and Gucun Park.

Lantern Festival at Shanghai City God Temple
Winter (December to February) in Shanghai is cold and damp. It rarely sees snow and mainly experiences rain.
Despite the cold, winter offers two big advantages: costs are generally about 30% lower than normal, and crowds are the thinnest of the year—except around late December (Christmas and New Year celebrations) and early February (Chinese New Year).
Aim for December if winter is your only option, when it is a festive month and the days are not that cold, which means you may still witness Shanghai's beautiful foliage.
As for January and February, the coldest months, it is better to focus on indoor activities with heating, such as admiring ancient bronzes at the Shanghai Museum, marveling at the stunning Jade Buddha at the Jade Buddha Temple, and attending a cooking class in a traditional longtang home.

Summer (June to August) is Shanghai's hottest, rainiest, and most typhoon-prone season, with average monthly rainfall of 5.2 inches and temperatures around 80°F (27°C).
Early to mid-June is your best window, when the temperatures and crowds haven't peaked yet, and rain is less frequent.
July is the hottest and most crowded month. Expect significant increases in hotel and airfare prices, as well as large crowds at attractions.
August is slightly cooler and less crowded than July, but typhoons are more likely and can affect flights. Be sure to check weather forecasts carefully and plan accordingly.

title: Shanghai Weather in October 2026: Mild, Sunny, Golden Week
text:
Home
 Destinations

Shanghai Weather in October 2026: Mild, Sunny, Golden Week
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated May. 8, 2026 
October is one of the best months of the year to visit Shanghai. Sunny days are the norm, with mild temperatures, low humidity, and little rain, making it ideal for outdoor exploration.
Expect average temperatures to range from 16°C (61°F) to 22°C (72°F), with about six rainy days bringing 56 mm (2.2 inches) of precipitation. Evenings are cooler, typically dropping to 13–15°C (55–59°F).
There is no need to worry about typhoons, since the typhoon season is typically over by October, unlike in August, with higher risks.
Is October a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?
Yes, we always recommend this period to our clients for its generally great weather. But with flexible dates, you can do even better.
Here's an insider tip: October is a month of two halves.
If you want the most reliably mild weather with fewer people, aim for mid-to-late October. For the best balance of comfort and value, this is your clear winner.
Early October (October 1–7) coincides with China's National Day holiday, which is one of the busiest times of the entire year.
Attractions are packed, and hotel rates, flights, and tickets all spike. Based on recent weather patterns, daytime temperatures can still feel like late summer (Shanghai reached 36°C / 97°F on October 6, 2025). Evenings cool down quickly, so layers are essential.
From mid-October through the end of the month, the weather settles into its most comfortable rhythm. Daytime highs hover around 20–22°C (68–72°F), nights are crisp but not cold, and humidity stays low. The crowds have also thinned out after the holiday.
Tips for Traveling During China's National Day Holiday
Normally, we suggest avoiding the Golden Week of October (October 1–7) for a better experience. However, if your travel dates are fixed, these practical tips could be helpful.
1. Book Everything Well in Advance
Don't wait until the last minute for a trip during the Golden Week. Hotels, flights, train tickets, and popular attraction admissions can sell out weeks before the holiday.  
Secure your reservations at least 1 month ahead, and for top spots like Shanghai Disneyland or Yu Garden, book as soon as tickets are released.
2. Travel During October 5–7 for Smaller Crowds
If your schedule allows, start your Shanghai trip on the 5th or 6th for much fewer people. 
The first four days of the holiday (October 1st to 4th) are the most crowded. By October 5th, many tourists from other places begin their return journeys, and Shanghai becomes noticeably quieter.
8-Day Shanghai, Hangzhou, Suzhou Family TourShanghai-Hangzhou-Wuzhen-Suzhou 
3. Avoid Peak Travel Days When Entering or Leaving Shanghai
The worst days for transportation are October 1-2 (arrivals) and October 6-7 (departures). Train stations and airports are overcrowded, and tickets are hardest to get. 
If you must travel on these dates, be sure to book your tickets in advance and allow ample time for check-in and security checks.
4. Swap Overcrowded Landmarks for Alternatives
Instead of struggling through the crowds in Zhujiajiao Water Town, head to Tongli Water Town, which is quieter, more authentic, and also close to Shanghai. 
For history enthusiasts, we suggest avoiding the long lines at the Shanghai Museum (East Branch) and visiting the Aurora Art Museum. The entrance fee is enough to deter a large portion of tourists who only visit free attractions, not to mention the museum's extensive collection of exquisite artifacts, allowing you to quietly appreciate the beauty of art.
If you want to enjoy a skyline view similar to the Bund but avoid crowds, head to the Sinar Mas Plaza on the North Bund, where you can grab a drink and admire the same iconic skyscrapers from a tranquil observation deck.
8-Day Beijing–Xi'an–Shanghai Tour China Golden Triangle
What to See and Do in Shanghai in October
Exhibits at the Aurora Museum
October's mild, dry weather makes almost every regular attraction in Shanghai enjoyable. 
The Bund, the French Concession, Yu Garden, and the water towns of Zhujiajiao or Tongli are all at their best without summer heat or winter chill. It's also a great time for observation decks on skyscrapers like the Shanghai Tower or Oriental Pearl Tower, where visibility is excellent.
And you also should not miss out on Shanghai Disneyland's Halloween season. From early October through the end of the month (October 4 to November 1 in 2025), the park transforms with pumpkin decorations, villains parade with Donald and Daisy Duck after nightfall, and you can meet Judy and Nick dressed in Halloween costumes in Zootopia.
4-Day Shanghai Family Disneyland Tour 
What to Pack and Wear in Shanghai in October
October in Shanghai brings comfortable mild days and crisp evenings. 
It is usually quite cool, but based on the weather data of 2025, early October can still feel like late summer, especially during the National Day holiday, so bring a few short-sleeved T-shirts and light pants.
Sunscreen and sunglasses are still useful, especially during sunny afternoons. Rain is rare, but a small folding umbrella doesn't hurt.
By mid-to-late October, daytime highs settle around 20–22°C (68–72°F), so pack with long-sleeved shirts and trousers.
Evenings in October are generally cool, sometimes to 13–15°C (55–59°F), so remember to take a mid-layer like a sweater or hoodie, and a windproof jacket with you, especially if you plan to take evening walks along the Bund or a Huangpu River night cruise.

Top 10 Things to Do in Shanghai
Shanghai, as the largest city in China, has the reputation of “the Paris of the East”. It is not only an economic center but also a famous cultural city with a deep modern urban culture and numerous historical sites. If you want to know about the modern China, Shanghai is a must-see place you need to visit. So what are the top 10 things to do in Shanghai? Where are the most interesting places to visit? Let’s have a look! 
1  
Exotic Building Clusters on the Bund
The Bund of Shanghai is located along the Huangpu River, with a total length of about 1.5 km (0.9 mile) from the Waibaidu Bridge to Nanpu Bridge, which is the most symbolic scenic spot of the city. The Exotic Building Clusters consists of 52 classical buildings of different architecture styles including Gothic, Baroque, Romanesque, Classicism and the Renaissance. These buildings were not from the same designer nor built in the same period, but they do have a unique harmonious beauty. One of the best things to do in Shanghai is to visit these resplendent buildings. You can experience the various art of architecture meanwhile knowing about China in modern times.
 Recommended Tour:  Shanghai 3 Days Tour with the Bund and Huangpu River from $509
2 
Night Cruise along Huangpu River
After seeing the Exotic Building Clusters, cruising along the Huangpu River can be a romantic thing to do in Shanghai at night. In the twilight, the neon lights shine on both sides and reflect each other, traveling on the Huangpu River by ship will give you a profound impression. On the east side, you can see modern skyscrapers. On the west side, you can appreciate the splendid Exotic Building Cluster in the distance. That will be a really unforgettable experience.
 Huangpu River Cruise Booking
3 
Overlooking the City from Shanghai Tower
In Pudong new area, stands the tallest building in China and the second tallest of the world, Shanghai Tower. The total height of the building is 632 meters (2,074 feet). The appearance of the building is spirally upward, symbolizing the shape of Chinese dragon. Standing on the 118-story sightseeing hall, you can have a close look at the Oriental Pearl Tower, Jin Mao Tower and the World Financial Center while overlooking the whole city. Thus you can understand why it lists on the top 10 things to do in Shanghai.
 Book a Shanghai Tower ticket.
4 
Have Fun in Shanghai Disneyland
Having fun in the Disneyland must be the best thing to do in Shanghai with kids. This is the first Disneyland Park on China’s mainland, which is located in Pudong new area. Here you can experience many "firsts" of the Disneyland including the largest Disney castle, the first pirate theme park and the longest Disney parade route. No matter, children and adults can find the joy in this magic kingdom. In addition, it is recommended to avoid peak hours such as holidays and weekends. If you can only go in these times, probably you will need to join long queues.
 Book Shanghai Disneyland Tickets.
5 
Shopping in Nanjing Road
Another must thing to do in Shanghai is shopping in Nanjing Road. From the West Yan'an Road in the west to the Bund in the east, the Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street lined with different shops stretches around 1,200 meters (1,312 yards). As the most prosperous street in Shanghai, here you can buy  products from all over the world. Besides the famous shopping malls, some classic restaurants of authentic local dishes can also be found. It is really a piece of good news for someone who has a passion for food. Walk to the end of Nanjing Road, you will reach the beautiful Bund.
6 
Yu Garden
Yu Garden is a classical, delicately designed garden with a history of more than 400 years. It’s one of the must-see places in Shanghai. The garden is not far from the Bund and the tranquil and beautiful environment is very attractive. Here you can see pavilions, rockeries and ponds in typical architecture style of South China gardens. Besides, you can appreciate the Chinese calligraphy and inscriptions of past masters. What’s more, Yuyuan Tourist Mart, outside of the garden, is a very busy district with various souvenirs and snacks.
 Recommended Tour:  Shanghai 1 Day Tour to Yu Garden from $109
 Book a Yu Garden Ticket.
7 
Tasting Local Snacks in City God Temple Area
If you are a foodie, then you are welcome to enjoy one of great but cheap things to do in Shanghai in the snack street near the Old City God Temple, which is connected to the Yuyuan Tourist Mart. You can taste nearly all kinds of local snacks here, such as Nanxiang Steamed Stuffed Buns, Chop Rice Cakes, Vegetable Stuffed Buns, Crab-Yellow Pastries and Cream Spiced Beans. And don’t forget the Fried Stuffed Buns, when eaten with Beef Vermicelli Soup, they're really delicious.
 Further Reading:  Top 10 Shanghai Street Food
8 
Tianzifang: Creative Leisure Block
Speaking of free things to do around Shanghai, Tianzifang is a must-see place. It is converted from the unique local Shikumen complex which is a type of traditional residence combining the western and Chinese characteristics. The block is the work base of many litterateurs and artists. There are some unique boutiques such as vintage glasses store and old-fashioned music boxes shop, as well as trendy clothing stores from Hong Kong. In addition, you can find some interesting and creative restaurants here. This place is certainly one of the best places to visit in Shanghai.
9 
Night Life in Hengshan Road
After a busy day's traveling, having a drink in Hengshan Road is one of the definite top things to do in Shanghai at night. As the most widely reputed street of leisure and entertainment in Shanghai, Hengshan Road is famous for the bars of different styles. Relaxing yourself and chatting with your friends here can be really enjoyable. In addition, on both sides of the road there are lush French sycamore trees and the distinctive upscale European buildings in the shade.
 Further Reading:  Shanghai Nightlife
10 
Zhujiajiao Water Town
Zhujiajiao, one of the city's four historic towns, is a definite place to visit near Shanghai. It is a typical ancient water town in the south of the Yangtze River. The town is crisscrossed with various water ways and there are several bridges with different shapes as well as numerous interesting stores. You can choose to stroll around the town on foot or by boat to experience the local customs and appreciate the ancient buildings. By the way, the traditional snacks are also very tasty.

As the locals in Shanghai put it, “Blessed are those born in Shanghai as they have the most chances to taste delicious food”. Shanghai is a multicultural city where people from different regions and with different cultural backgrounds gather, bringing their own culinary traditions. Nanjing Road
China's premier shopping street, the 5.5-km-long (3.4-mile-long) Nanjing Road, starts at the Bund in the east and ends in the west at the junction of Jing'an Temple and West Yan'an Street. Today it is a must-see metropolitan destination attracting thousands of fashion-seeking shoppers from all over the world. Nanjing Road, Shanghai
  Pictures     Video 
As a century-old shopping street in Huangpu District, Shanghai, Nanjing Road was a witness of the city's history. Over time, it has been restructured, undergoing significant changes. Big traditional stores no longer dominate the market since modern shopping malls, specialty stores, theaters, and international hotels have mushroomed on both sides of the street. For shopping convenience, its eastern end has an all-weather pedestrian arcade.
What to Do in Nanjing Road
 Shops along the Nanjing Road  
Exploring traditional department stores and latest fashion stores
Over 600 businesses on the road offer countless famous brands of superior quality and new fashions. Upscale stores include Tiffany, Mont Blanc, Omega, and Dunhill. Approximately a hundred traditional stores and specialty shops provide choice silk goods, jade, embroidery, wool, and clocks. Shopping lovers will immerse themselves in the joy of purchasing here.
Savoring snacks of time-horned brands
Century-old traditional food stores can be easily found on Nanjing Road. You cannot only taste the most authentic Shanghai food here, but also buy some for your friends and families as gifts.

Zhen Lao Da Fang: Selling smoked fish and moon cakes with meat fillings
Shanghai First Food Hall: Gathering various kinds of local snacks including traditional cakes

Taking the Dangdang sightseeing tram

Zhujiajiao Water Town
 Located in Qingpu District of Shanghai, Zhujiajiao Water Town, aka Zhujiajiao Water Village, is well-known throughout the country, with a history of more than 1,700 years. Covering an area of 47 square kilometers (11,614 acres), the little fan-shaped town, being regarded as Shanghai’s Venice, glimmers like a bright pearl in the landscape of lakes and mountains.
Endowed with another elegant name – “Pearl Stream” – the Zhujiajiao Ancient Water Town is the best-preserved among the four ancient towns in Shanghai. Unique old bridges across bubbling streams, small rivers shaded by willow trees, and houses with courtyards attached all transport people who have been living amidst the bustle and hustle of the modern big city to a brand-new world full of antiquity, leisure and tranquility. More Pictures Map of Zhujiajiao Water Town (Click to Enlarge)  
Top Activities and Attractions in Zhujiajiao Water Town
Explore Historic BridgesIt is said that to visit Zhujiajiao Water Town without seeing the bridges means that you have not really been to Zhujiajiao at all! Bridges here are distinctive with a long-standing history, built during Ming  (1368-1644) and Qing  (1636-1912) Dynasties. The antique Zhujiajiao Water Town is thoroughly connected by 36 delicate spans in different shapes and styles, from wooden to stone to marble.
Fangsheng Bridge (Setting-fish-free Bridge), built in 1571 by a monk after 15 years of begging for alms, used to be a place where Buddhist monks and pilgrims released aquatic animals at the very beginning. It is the longest, largest and tallest stone bridge in Shanghai region, with five arches. Hence, it has been hailed as “the No.1 Bridge in Shanghai”. On the bridge stands a stone tablet named Dragon Gate Stone, which is engraved with 8 coiling dragons encircling a shining pearl. On top of the bridge are 4 lifelike stone lions. Boats quietly glide through the bridge arches, complemented by the dark tiles and white walls, as well as the carved doors and windows of the ancient buildings on both sides of the river. Together they create harmonious scenes as if you’ve stepped into a dreamy old memory of southern China. It’s absolutely a perfect spot for stunning photos. Sightseeing Boats Fangsheng Bridge 
Lang Bridge (Veranda Bridge) is the only wooden bridge and the most featured span in Zhujiajiao Water Town. The exposed parts of its main structure, including the bridge deck, beams, columns and railings, are all made of wood and retain the traditional mortise-and-tenon craftsmanship. Due to the roof on the bridge with upturned eaves and its elegant and simple style, it resembles a narrow corridor. During the Qianlong reign of the Qing Dynasty (1736-1796), the main streets on both sides of the river here became increasingly prosperous, but people could only travel between the streets by detour, causing inconvenience to trade and daily life. Therefore, the local people built this bridge to connect the two banks of the river, bringing many benefits. On a sunny day, if you’re looking for a cool, shaded spot to enjoy the view of Zhujiajiao Water Town, this is an optimal place.
Ride a Traditional Black-awning BoatComing to Zhujiajiao Water Town, riding the traditional black-awning boat is an unmissable experience. If you are not in a rush, just escape from the bustling crowds elsewhere and sit in the boat, enjoying the gentle breeze and graceful residential buildings on both banks passing by in front of your eyes. There are mainly two options. One is that you can enter the town by taking the boat outside near the Zhujiajiao Metro Station of Line 17, which costs USD 6 per person. The second option is to take a boat tour inside the ancient town. There are three docks located at Kezhi Garden, City God Temple, and North Street. Each boat holds a maximum of 6 people, with a ride duration of 15-20 minutes and a cost of USD 30-45 per boat. You may share the boat with other tourists, which is much more cost-effective.
Stroll Along North Street and Try Local Snacks Narrow Lanes in the Town In the northern part of Zhujiajiao Water Town, there is a quaint and historic street, namely, the North Street, which features representative and elegant ancient buildings from the Ming and Qing Dynasties. Although only about one kilometer (0.62 miles) long, it is the one of the best-preserved ancient streets in Shanghai. The Street is only 3 to 4 meters (3.5 to 13 feet) wide, narrowing to just 2 meters (7 feet) at its narrowest point. The overhanging eaves of the houses on both sides form a unique “sky slit” view. Strolling on this ancient place and appreciating the historic buildings, as well as the many narrow lanes is truly a delightful experience.
Most importantly, the street is lined with long-established stores and exudes pleasant aroma of diversified local food, making it a great place to grab lunch and snacks. Sticky rice dumplings, braised pork, and various pastries made with black sesame and nuts are all worth trying.
Visit Elegant GardensThe ancient water town is also famous for the imposing gardens. The largest manorial one in this region is called Kezhi Garden, whose name stands for two aspects of virtues: cultivating oneself by reading and overcome hardships through agricultural practices. Stepping inside, you can appreciate classical elements of Chinese garden embodied in ponds, rockeries, pavilions, zigzag bridge, tower, etc.  
Next to Kezhi Garden nestles another one—Hexin Garden. It is a relatively quiet small garden, but its interior landscape is truly remarkable, making it an ideal place for you to enjoy the scenery while temporarily escaping from the crowds. The garden houses many antiques from the Ming and Qing dynasties, such as the Rosewood Cabinet with Cloud-and-Dragon Carvings and the Twelve-Panel Huanghuali Screen, allowing you to appreciate the scenery while feeling as if you are visiting a museum. Moreover, the garden frequently hosts opera performances like Kunqu Opera, providing a great delight for tourists who love Chinese opera.
Visit the Great Qing Post OfficeIt is the site of the former Great Qing Post Office established in 1903. The office is a two-story European-style building, with dark-red brick walls and an exquisite mailbox at the front door that has witnessed the development history of Shanghai into a first-class metropolis. The first floor is a free area where you can experience making your own postcards with vintage postmarks and admire various cultural and creative products. The second floor is an exhibition area introducing the postal services of multiple dynasties and displaying precious postcards and original letters in the past.
How to Tour the Zhujiajiao Water Town?Recommended visit time: 3-4 hours City God Temple 
Enter the ancient town from the entrance and follow the river all the way. You can visit the top scenic spots while enjoying snacks and drinks along the path. If you get tired, just choose to relax in the peaceful, slow boat ride.
Suppose you’re not time-pressed, you can also visit the gardens to experience the cultural atmosphere, or explore the time-honored stores in the alleys to feel the local customs and lifestyle. At sunset, as the town’s lanterns light up one by one, you’re recommended to stay for a while, enjoying the gentle and romantic scene where the sunset glow, lanterns and water reflect beautifully on each other.
How to get to Zhujiajiao Water Town from Shanghai Downtown?
By MetroYou can take Metro Line 17 and get off at Zhujiajiao Station, and then walk north for about 15-20 minutes to arrive the town. 
Or if you don’t want to walk for such a long time, you can take Bus No. 1510 here at the metro station, which is the tourist bus directly to Zhujiajiao Water Town. Another solution is to ride a boat at the dock near Zhujiajiao Metro Station into the town.
By TaxiStarting from People’s Square or Nanjing Road in downtown Shanghai, it is about 48 kilometers (30 miles) to Zhujiajiao Ancient Town. If you don’t want to transfer between transportation modes and prefer a direct trip, taking a taxi would be a better choice. The journey will take approximately 1.5 hours, with a fare ranging from USD 20-25.
Does Zhujiajiao Water Town Require a Ticket?Visitors are exempted from the entrance fees of Zhujiajiao Water Town. However, they are required to buy the tickets for visiting some specific attractions inside it. Below are some combo tickets: Price Type USD 12 Kezhi Garden + Hexin Garden + Shanghai Helong Art Gallery + Shanghai Handicraft Zhujiajiao Exhibition Hall + City God Temple + Yuanjin Buddhist Temple + Quanhua Museum USD 6 Kezhi Garden + City God Temple + Yuanjin Buddhist Temple + Shanghai Handicraft Zhujiajiao Exhibition Hall
 Deposit: CNY 400 or 50 US dollars, or a passport USD 9 Kezhi Garden + Hexin Garden + Shanghai Helong Art Gallery + Quanhua Museum Note: Free for children below 1.3 meters (4.3 feet) 
 Zhujiajiao Water Town Ticket Booking
Opening HoursThe town is open all day, but some of its attractions, such as the Kezhi Garden, the Qing Dynasty Post Office, and the City God Temple, etc. are usually open from 08:30 to 17:00, and last entry is at 16:30.
Travel Tips1. Wear comfortable shoes since you have to keep walking around the town. 
2. If you plan to visit Zhujiajiao Ancient Town in the summer (June-August), remember to bring mosquito patches or spray. Due to the hot and humid weather during this season, mosquitoes are especially active in the waterside areas of the town from dusk till night.

Pudong New Area, Shanghai
Pudong New Area Facts
Chinese Name: 浦东新区 (pǔ dōng xīn qū)
Population: 5,501,000
Area: 1,210 square kilometers (467.2 square miles)
Location: in the east of Shanghai City, east China
Area Code: 021
Zip Code: 200120
GDP (2018): CNY 1,046 billion (USD 158.1 billion)
First Free Trade Pilot Zone in China
Pudong New Area is a municipal district of Shanghai City. Fengxian District and Minhang District are on its north. Xuhui District, Huangpu District, Hongkou District, Yangpu District and Baoshan District are to its west across the Huangpu River. Chongming District is on its north. Pudong New Area Shanghai is the first free trade pilot zone in China. It is rich in tourism attractions including Chuansha Ancient Town, Shanghai Wild Animal Park and the Oriental Pearl Radio & TV Tower.
Best Places to Visit & Top Things to Do in Pudong New AreaYou may need 1-2 days for Pudong New Area travel in modern skyscrapers, Chuansha Ancient Town, Shanghai Wild Animal Park, Shanghai Science Center and other tourism attractions.
Visit Modern Skyscrapers
 Skyscrapers in Pudong 
 Shanghai Tower
As the highest skyscraper in Shanghai, it is 632 meters (2,073 feet) high with 119 floors. Travelers can overlook the whole city on the 118th floor and enjoy the light show on holidays.
 Shanghai World Financial Center
Located in Lujiazui, it is 492 meters (1,614 feet) high with 101 floors above ground. Travelers can go sightseeing on 94th – 100th floor. And the high-speed elevator is with a maximum speed of 8 meters per second which only takes 66 seconds to the 95th floor.
 Oriental Pearl Tower
It is one of the iconic cultural landscapes in Shanghai. Travelers can have a full view of the city on the sightseeing floor, have delicious dishes in the revolving restaurant and experience the unique Shanghai culture in the exhibition hall.
 Jin Mao Tower
With 420.5 meters (1,780 feet) high, there are 88 floors of the main building and the sightseeing hall is on the top. The outer wall is made up of large glasses which reflect in different shades and colors.
Shanghai Wild Animal ParkIt is the first national grade wild zoo in China. Travelers can see more than 200 kinds of rare wild animals from home and abroad such as pandas, monkeys, zebras, and white rhinoceros. You should pay attention to that spring from March to May and autumn from September to November are the best time to visit safari park.
Chuansha Ancient TownChuansga is the hometown of Shanghai Opera, a gathering place for opera fans. With more than 500-year-history, Chuansha Ancient Town still remains an ancient wall from the Ming Dynasty (1368 – 1644). There is a great combination of western and Chinese elements, such as the Catholic Church which will leave you a deep impression.
Others: Long Museum
Best Time to Visit Pudong New AreaThe best time to visit Pudong New Area is from March to May and from September to November with a temperature of 15-21℃ (59-69.8℉). It is located in the coastal area where the East Asian monsoon prevails, and the climate in Pudong New Area Shanghai belongs to the subtropical monsoon climate. With distinct four seasons, there are abundant rainfalls, sufficient sunshine and suitable temperature. The annual average temperature is 16℃ (61℉). You should pay attention to that from April to September is the rainy season.
During March and May, the peach blossoms will be in full bloom, it is the best time to admire the beauty of flowers.
Pudong Weather Forecast
-
TransportationShanghai Pudong International Airport is located in Pudong New Area, about 40 km (24.9 mi) and Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport is about 30 km (18.6 mi) from the center area of Pudong New Area. Travelers can choose to take a flight to these two airports first and then take Metro Line 2 to Pudong New Area. Shanghai Railway Station and Shanghai South Railway Station are very close to Pudong New Area, travelers can take Metro Line 1 and transfer Line 2 after getting off the train.
Within the city area, Metro Line 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 16 are available. The taxi charges CNY 14 for the first 3 km, CNY 2.4/km for no more than 10 km, and CNY 3.6/km for subsequent distance. It may cost CNY 140-150 from Shanghai Pudong International Airport and CNY 60-70 from Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport to Pudong New Area.
 See more: Shanghai Metro, Shanghai Taxi
Pudong Food to TryThere are many delicious local foods in Pudong New Area including Sanlin Benggua, Gaoqiao Waffle, Pan-Fried Chicken Bun, and White Rabbit Sugar.
 Sanlin Benggua
This kind of melon is in an oblong shape with a weight of 1-1.5 kg. The melon rind is very thin and crispy. It is famous for its sweet taste.
 Gaoqiao Waffle
It is famous for its well-bedded pastries which are as thin as paper. It is shaped like a moon cake with a fragrant flavor, thin skin, various stuffing, crispy and soft taste.
 Pan-Fried Chicken Bun
With yellow sesame seeds and chopped green onion in the upper part, it tastes soft and palatable. And the lower part is crispier with heavy stuffing and juicy chicken.

Shanghai Weather in September
 From early to late September, Shanghai weather transitions from stuffy to a bit cool. As for rainfall, showers occur frequently but don’t significantly impact travel; besides, there is a relatively high probability of a typhoon striking, especially around the middle of the month. It may not be a perfect time to visit Shanghai. That said, September is a rare time when Shanghai isn’t overly crowded, except around the Mid-Autumn Festival. Zhujiajiao View in September  
Hot First Half Month and Cooler Second HalfTraveling to Shanghai in the first half of September, you will basically have hot and not very comfortable experiences during your outdoor visits, especially in the daytime. Generally speaking, Shanghai is still in summer at this time, and the daily high temperature is mainly in the range of 30-35 degrees Celsius (86-95 degrees Fahrenheit) and reaches 36-38°C (97-100°F) occasionally. On top of that, the humid air makes the weather muggy. Nighttime tours are indeed a little more comfortable than daytime ones, but don’t expect the weather to turn cool: the daily low is at 25-28°C (68-82°F), and on sunny days, the temperature is still high at around 30°C (86°F) at 21:00.
Entering the second half month, the temperature shows a downward trend. Most of the time, the daily high and low hovers around 30°C (86°F) and 23°C (73°F), respectively, indicating that you will no longer feel uncomfortably hot at that time. Note that exceptions may exist, for instance, in 2025, several days in late September still experienced hot daytime with the high temperature of 34-35°C (93-95°F). Visitors in Shanghai in Hot Early September  
Showers Fall Frequently, and Typhoon May OccurRain falls frequently this month in Shanghai: there are 13 rainy days on average. Fortunately, not all of them will influence your trip.
Most of the time, the rain comes and stops quickly and usually in the afternoon, though sometimes heavy. In other words, when encountering rain during your tour this month, you can head to a cafe to take shelter from the rain. Then, maybe 30 minutes later, the sun will reappear, and you can continue your outdoor visit. Moreover, this kind of rain may bring temperature drops and bring a sense of coolness.
Note that the rainfalls caused by typhoons are different. Usually, the typhoon brings long-duration and high-intensity rain, during which you may need to stop your visit and stay in your hotel for safety. Over the past five years, Shanghai experienced three direct typhoon landfalls in September, and all in mid-month.
Daylight Hours & UV RaysDaylight hours are shortening from 12.5 to 11.5 this month. If you have a packed itinerary and want to have a rest at noon, you are recommended to get up early each day to gain enough visiting time, especially if your visiting dates are in late September.
UV index is high at 9 in Shanghai in September, making sun-protection measures necessary during the sunshine hours, which average 6 hours per day.

Air Quality in September

What to Wear in Shanghai in September？  Clothes: During the first half month, outfits like T-shirts plus skirts, short shirts plus shorts, and dresses are good choices. If you are worried about feeling cold in air-conditioned places like the metro, just bring a light jacket. 
Traveling to Shanghai during the second half month, especially the final days of the month, thin long pants are better choices than shorts. If girls want to wear skirts, longer ones are more recommended. Besides, add thin baseball jackets or long-sleeved shirts in the morning and evening. 
 Shoes: Sandals are OK in the first half month, while thin sneakers and casual shoes are more proper in the second half month.
 Others: Umbrella, sunglasses, and hats.
Crowds of Shanghai in SeptemberIn 2027, the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday will fall on September 15th, and then, three days later, the National Day holiday will begin. So, starting late September, you can expect extremely large crowds and quite high hotel prices in Shanghai. 
However, in the other time of September, Shanghai is in its shoulder season. You can have relatively quiet experiences in attractions like the Yu Garden and the Bund, wait in short lines for popular items in the Disneyland Park, and have a budget-friendly trip. Tranquil Yu Garden in September  
Tips for Traveling to Shanghai in SeptemberNo matter when you visit Shanghai, you will include some of the most popular attractions like the exquisite Yu Garden, the modern and dazzling Bund, the lively Nanjing Road, and the Shanghai Museum with a rich collection. However, you should plan your itinerary carefully to ensure a more comfortable and enjoyable trip.
Tips for Tours in Early SeptemberFor trips during this period, the biggest challenge will be the high heat. You are recommended to plan outdoor visits, such as exploring Yu Garden, in early morning. Then, during the hottest hours from 12:00-15:00, you can visit indoor attractions like the Shanghai Museum to keep cool. After that, when the heat gradually disappears, you can explore the Nanjing Road and go to the Bund to experience a beautiful sunset and the dazzling night view. Dazzling Night View  
Tips for Tours in Mid-SeptemberSpecial attention should be paid to the weather forecast to monitor whether there is a typhoon during your stay - this period is the peak season for typhoons. If there will be direct hit of a typhoon, you may want to advance or postpone your trip. So, you are advised to book hotels that can be canceled for free. If Shanghai is predicted to be affected only by the outer bands of a typhoon and you still plan to visit Shanghai during this period, you may want to add more indoor attractions to your travel list. 
Tips for Tours in Late SeptemberClimate of Shanghai turns better at this time: it is no longer very hot, and the peak typhoon season ends. So, you are prone to gaining a better travel experience during this period.
However, in 2027, if your travel days include September 15, the Mid-Autumn Festival Holiday, be sure to make related reservations in advance and be prepared for the higher travel expense. Besides, begin your daily trip early to avoid the main crowds. 
Travel Highlights of Shanghai in September
1. Shanghai Tourism FestivalIt is a major cultural and tourism event held in Shanghai every September. During the festival, numerous activities are organized. Among them, the most lively, spectacular, and unmissable event is the parade of performance troupes and floats that kicks off the festival on the Bund on opening day. In addition, every evening during the festival, the Huangpu River is illuminated by a series of dazzling light shows.
2. Mid-Autumn Festival EventsFor Chinese people, the Mid-Autumn Festival is an important time for family reunion, during which many attractions in Shanghai will host celebratory events. For instance, the Yu Garden and Guyi Garden will be decorated with beautiful lanterns, and the Disneyland Park will have some festival-related performances and delicacies.

上海住宿區域地圖
第一次來上海自由行，強烈建議沿著地鐵 2 號線（綠線）找住宿。這條黃金線路貫穿了虹橋機場、浦東機場，並直達南京西路、人民廣場、南京東路與陸家嘴等核心地標，對於拖著行李的旅客來說最省力。
南京路 / 人民廣場：地鐵樞紐，生活機能最強
這裡是上海的門面，也是交通的大動脈（地鐵 1, 2, 8, 10 號線交匯）。住在這裡幾乎不用操心交通，下樓就是步行街、百貨商場與老字號排隊美食（如：佳家湯包、大壺春、沈大成）。
✅ 優點： 交通樞紐地位無可取代，機場直達免轉車；生活機能最強，深夜宵夜選擇多。
❌ 缺點： 觀光客人潮極多，環境較吵雜；熱門飯店在尖峰時段等電梯或入住排隊較久。
💡 私房建議： 優先選「南京東路站」附近的飯店，走路到外灘僅需 10-15 分鐘，晚上散步回房還能省下排隊等計程車的時間。
外灘區：經典海派情懷，沉浸式夜景
外灘（The Bund）是上海的靈魂。這裡有許多由百年老建築改建的頂級奢華飯店（如：和平飯店、華爾道夫），或是對望陸家嘴摩天大樓的新潮飯店（如：W 酒店、艾迪遜）。
✅ 優點： 坐擁世界級「一線江景」，拍照打卡極美；海派奢華氛圍感十足，求婚、慶生首選。
❌ 缺點： 房價通常是全上海天花板；飯店離地鐵站通常有段距離（需走 10 分鐘以上），出入較依賴叫車。
💡 私房建議： 預算夠一定要訂「江景房」！能避開江邊人擠人的喧囂，在房間喝咖啡看東方明珠，才是最奢華的上海享受。
靜安區：最道地的上海時髦感
如果你不愛商業感太重，靜安區是深度旅遊的首選。這裡有許多梧桐樹街道、老洋房改建的精品飯店，能體驗到最有氣質的上海生活。
✅ 優點： 觀光客相對較少，環境精緻安靜；周邊佈滿精品店與文青咖啡廳，是 Citywalk 的天堂。
❌ 缺點： 離外灘、陸家嘴等必去景點稍遠；部分地段位於巷弄內，大型行李移動較費力。
💡 私房建議： 選在「靜安寺站」附近，轉乘方便且離網紅街道「武康路、安福路」很近，非常適合喜歡慢節奏、愛拍照的旅人。
浦東 / 陸家嘴：迪士尼迷與商務首選
浦東飯店普遍較新、空間寬敞，適合重視住宿硬體的旅客。如果你打算去上海迪士尼，住浦東能省下不少車程；此外，從浦東看回浦西外灘的建築群，視野更加遼闊。
✅ 優點： 飯店設施新、房間坪數大、行政服務好；離迪士尼與機場較近，親子遊客首選。
❌ 缺點： 商業氣息重，缺少老上海的煙火氣；前往浦西老城區（如豫園、新天地）需跨江，搭地鐵較耗時。
💡 私房建議： 浦東飯店的五星級飯店（如麗思卡爾頓、文華東方）通常硬體維護得更好，如果很在意泳池、健身房或 SPA 品質，選浦東不會出錯。

上海住宿區域房價？
上海住宿的房價分布很廣，舉例來說，市中心的三星級飯店雙人房，價格多半從 台幣 2,000 ～3,000元起跳；如果想住得高級一點，五星級飯店多從台幣6,000 元起，熱門飯店甚至會更高。碰到旅遊旺季或節假日，房價通常會上漲不少，建議一定要提早預訂才有機會搶到好位置、好價格。在上海市區找住宿，最重要的就是交通便利性，最好選擇靠近地鐵站，這樣不管是逛街、吃美食還是跑景點都超方便！
上海住宿
1. 上海南京路假日酒店 (Holiday Inn Shanghai Nanjing Road By IHG)
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$3,800左右
｜Agoda優惠價｜Booking訂房｜Klook預訂
｜交通：搭乘地鐵抵達「南京東路站/人民廣場站」，出站後走路8~10分鐘
｜親子入住：0至2歲(含)嬰幼兒，在不加床之情況下可免費與大人同住。
上海南京路假日酒店近期有重新裝修過，地點超方便，走路就能到南京路、外灘，附近還有超多美食跟奶茶店。地鐵2號線跟10號線就在附近，要去哪都超快。
服務人員超親切，不管櫃檯還是清潔阿姨都很有禮貌、笑容滿滿。
床真的超級好睡，軟硬適中，一覺到天亮比我家床還舒服！
早餐選擇比想像中豐富，竟然還有免費洗衣房跟烘衣機，超貼心！
高樓層景觀超讚，房間一打開窗就是美景，晚上看夜景超療癒。
缺點： 飯店歷史較久，雖然有翻新但部分隔音稍弱。地點雖好但門口計程車較難開入，建議搭地鐵。
2. 上海康萊德酒店 (Conrad Shanghai)
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$5,000左右
｜Agoda優惠價｜Booking訂房｜Klook預訂
｜交通：搭乘地鐵抵達「人民廣場站」，出站後走路4分鐘；如果開車的話，有免費停車場
｜親子入住：7歲(含)以上兒童依大人標準收費。
地點無敵方便，樓下就是人民廣場站，走幾步就到南京路步行街。
房間乾淨又舒適，空間夠大、採光很好，住起來非常放鬆。
高樓層景觀，打開窗戶就能看到外灘或南京路，夜景超迷人。
親子友善細節做得好，連奶嘴都會墊杯墊晾乾，這服務真的很加分。
整體環境安靜舒適，雖然在熱鬧地段，但房間內完全不吵，睡得超好。
3. 上海艾迪遜酒店 (The Shanghai EDITION)
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$9,000左右
｜Agoda優惠價｜Booking訂房｜Klook預訂
｜交通：搭乘地鐵抵達「南京東路站」，出站後走路2分鐘；如果開車的話，有免費停車場
｜親子入住：12歲(含)以上兒童依大人標準收費
地點真的超棒，樓下就是南京東路，走路5分鐘就能到外灘，去哪都超方便。
房間設計簡約高級又舒適，空間寬敞、床超好睡，完全不想起來
房間景色絕美，景觀房的落地窗看出去就能看到東方明珠和黃浦江，晚上夜景超療癒。
屋頂酒吧超有氣氛，29樓Punch Room的夜景超震撼，還有熱情的店員幫拍美照！
早餐現點現做、選擇豐富，蝦仁炒飯、咖哩牛肉、牛肉粉絲湯每樣都好吃
4. 上海雅居樂萬豪侯爵酒店 (Shanghai Marriott Marquis City Centre)
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$4,700左右
｜Agoda優惠價｜Booking訂房｜Klook預訂
｜交通：搭乘地鐵抵達「人民廣場站」，出站後走路8分鐘；如果開車的話，有付費停車場
｜親子入住：0-2 歲，在不佔床之情況下可免費與大人同住
地理位置超棒，就在南京東路和人民廣場旁邊，去哪都方便！
附近吃喝超方便，樓下就有瑞幸咖啡、麥當勞、便利店，宵夜也不怕餓到。
高樓層景觀好驚艷，大片落地窗望出去就是城市天際線，夜景超美。
早餐選擇豐富又好吃，中式西式都有，還有貼心外帶服務。
房間寬敞乾淨，住三晚都睡得超好，設備雖然不新但保養得不錯。
5. 上海璞麗酒店 (The PuLi Hotel and Spa)
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$8,100左右
｜Agoda優惠價｜Booking訂房｜Klook預訂
｜交通：搭乘地鐵抵達「靜安寺」，出站後走路2分鐘；如果開車的話，有付費停車場
｜親子入住：0-2 歲，在不佔床之情況下可免費與大人同住
地理位置方便，離靜安寺地鐵站走路只要一分鐘，逛街用餐都超方便。
飯店設計感十足，Jaya操刀的東方禪意風格，在靜安區營造鬧中取靜。
整體氛圍低調奢華，有歷史的氣質感，不像一般新飯店那樣浮誇，反而更讓人著迷。
景觀超美，還能看到靜安公園或城市夜景，尤其高樓層夜晚特別有氣氛。
房內迷你吧免費還有香檳紅酒，完全是驚喜感爆棚，質感滿滿。
早餐質感高、窗外綠意盎然，雖然選項不多但每樣都好吃又精緻。
6. 上海豫園萬麗酒店 (Renaissance Shanghai Yu Garden Hotel on the Bund)
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$3,900左右
｜Agoda優惠價｜Booking訂房｜Klook預訂
｜交通：搭乘地鐵抵達「豫園站」，出站後走路1分鐘；如果開車的話，有免費停車場
｜親子入住：13歲(含)以上兒童依大人標準收費
地點超級方便，出門就是地鐵站，走路就能到豫園、城隍廟和外灘，觀光無敵順路！
房間寬敞又乾淨，遮光好、隔音好，連續住幾晚都睡得很舒服。高樓層的房間能直接看到東方明珠和黃浦江，夜景超迷人。
早餐中西皆有選擇，還有行政酒廊下午茶可以吃點心、小酌一杯超享受。
親子友善很加分，有佈置可愛的親子房型，孩子還收到伴手禮超開心。
泡澡放鬆好療癒，房間有浴缸加上水壓強，洗一場熱水澡超舒壓。
7. 上海浦東麗思卡爾頓酒店 (The Ritz-Carlton Shanghai, Pudong)
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$10,000左右
｜Agoda優惠價｜Booking訂房｜Klook預訂
｜交通：搭乘地鐵抵達「陸家嘴站」，出站後走路3分鐘；如果開車的話，有付費停車場
｜親子入住：12歲(含)以上兒童依大人標準收費。
位置便利，就在陸家嘴國金中心，樓下就是商場、星巴克、迪士尼旗艦店，逛街吃飯都方便。
房間舒適又有質感，躺在懶人椅上看風景超愜意，裝潢走典雅奢華路線。房間內從床墊、寢具、備品到每個服務小細節都精緻講究。
景觀真的無敵，房間直接對望東方明珠和黃浦江，夜晚燈火璀璨美到捨不得睡！
設施一應俱全，SPA、泳池、健身房、酒吧樣樣都有，房間有免治馬桶。
頂樓 Flair Bar 必訪，氣氛超好、景色絕美，是喝酒看夜景的神級地方。
8. 上海外灘W酒店 (W Shanghai – The Bund)
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$9,000左右
｜Agoda優惠價｜Booking訂房｜Klook預訂
｜交通：搭乘地鐵抵達「國際客運中心站」，出站後走路2分鐘；如果開車的話，有免費停車場
｜親子入住：12歲(含)以上兒童依大人標準收費。
景觀超級震撼，景觀房落地窗一打開就是東方明珠和外灘三大高樓，白天夜晚都超有感。
地點真的太方便了，出門就到北外灘，樓下就是白玉蘭廣場，美食跟景點全包。
房間設計年輕時尚又有氛圍感，燈光、香氛、床都讓人有在派對的錯覺。
戶外泳池景色一流，邊游泳邊看浦東夜景，整個人chill到不行。
早餐超豐盛、還能延長到11點，各種肉類、現做料理都有，吃得超滿足。
缺點： 音樂較大聲、風格前衛，適合年輕人，不一定適合喜歡傳統靜謐長輩。
9. 上海浦東文華東方酒店 (Mandarin Oriental Pudong Shanghai)
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$6,200左右
｜Agoda優惠價｜Booking訂房｜Klook預訂
｜交通：搭乘地鐵抵達「陸家嘴站」，出站後走路15分鐘；如果開車的話，有免費停車場
｜親子入住：12歲(含)以上兒童依大人標準收費
江景視野超美，窗外直接看到東方明珠和黃浦江，不管白天或夜晚都超享受。
房間設備智慧又實用，從燈光、溫濕度控制、文具、防水袋、洗衣回收，全都幫你想到。
房間超寬敞又好睡，床品是定製的，香氛淡雅，泡澡用大浴缸真的太享受。
早餐豐盛又不擁擠，不只西式選擇多，中式鍋貼還有驚喜，還能外帶到房內用餐超方便。
設施雖老但維護得很好，泳池、三溫暖、健身房都很乾淨，
缺點： 離最近的地鐵站「陸家嘴站」或「浦東南路站」走路較遠（約15分鐘），建議出入叫車。
10. 上海半島酒店 (The Peninsula Shanghai)
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$11,800左右
｜Agoda優惠價｜Booking訂房｜Klook預訂
｜交通：搭乘地鐵抵達「南京東路站」，出站後走路10分鐘；如果開車的話，有免費停車場
｜親子入住：12 歲（含）以上的孩童將依成人價格收費。
地點好，一出門就是外灘，步行幾分鐘就能到外白渡橋和其他景點。
服務真的頂級貼心，從門口迎賓到客房安排，所有員工都記得我們姓氏，太暖了！
房間設計高雅又智能，不只動線合理，連濕度、燈光、窗簾都能細調整，一進房就不想出門。
早餐出乎意料地精緻又好吃，鍋貼皮酥餡香，班尼迪克蛋也超有水準，每天都吃得超滿足。
景觀超夢幻，選了招牌江景房，東方明珠、黃浦江盡收眼底，夜景根本像電影畫面。
上海住宿-上海迪士尼飯店
上海迪士尼樂園內有2家官方主題飯店，分別是上海迪士尼樂園酒店、玩具總動員酒店。
上海迪士尼樂園酒店
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$13,000左右
｜Trip.com優惠價｜Klook優惠
｜交通：搭地鐵直接搭到迪士尼站，出站後搭乘迪士尼度假區穿梭巴士，直接抵達酒店；如果開車的話，有提供免費住客停車場
｜親子入住：0-2歲兒童，在不佔床之情況下可免費與大人同住
飯店有免費的渡輪和接駁巴士，接駁巴士從飯店門口上車，直達迪士尼小鎮入口，從早上 7 點開始運行，第一班很容易搶到。
如果你不趕時間，推薦坐船前往樂園，可以欣賞星願湖的景色，還有專屬飯店房卡通道，不要忘記攜帶房卡哦！
床墊軟硬適中，還有專門為小朋友準備的小童枕頭，累了一天能夠一覺到天亮。還有可愛的迪士尼洗浴用品，連嬰兒沐浴乳都有！
泳池乾淨，維護良好：水質清澈，還有專人隨時打掃甲板上的水漬，提供免費毛巾＆水瓶。
早餐菜色有米奇鬆餅、香腸、雞蛋等西式選擇，最棒的是迪士尼角色(米奇、米妮、布魯托、高飛)會來互動！
玩具總動員酒店
｜雙人房低價位：TWD$7,100左右
｜Agoda優惠價｜Trip.com優惠價｜Klook優惠
｜交通：搭地鐵直接搭到迪士尼站，出站後搭乘迪士尼度假區穿梭巴士，直接抵達酒店；如果開車的話，有提供免費住客停車場
｜親子入住：0-2歲兒童，在不佔床之情況下可免費與大人同住
住這裡的超大福利—提前入園，省去排長隊的煩惱！清晨巴士直達樂園門口，不用繞大圈！
接駁巴士的安排很密集，酒店往返迪士尼小鎮每十分鐘一班，往返樂園酒店和地鐵站則是十五分鐘一班。遇到提早入園和樂園散場時會加開班次
房間不算大，但細節滿滿，隨處可見巴斯光年&胡迪！電視可看超多迪士尼動畫，可以開心追劇到天亮！
工作人員態度友善、熱情，特別照顧親子旅客！行李寄放很周到，入住時直接有條碼，行李會送到房間！
酒店還有提供巴斯光年叫醒服務，預訂後早上巴斯光年會在房間裡叫你起床，小朋友特別喜歡，整體體驗很有趣。
如果是入住酒店的客人，推薦在禮賓部購買半日票，下午三點就能進樂園，適合懶人行程。
上海住宿常見問題
Q1：第一次來上海自由行，住哪間飯店「地鐵交通最省力、出門下樓就能吃喝採買」？
A：唯一首推地鐵人民廣場站正上方的「上海康莱德酒店（上海康萊德酒店）」！1、2、8 號線三鐵交會出站即達，下樓即是南京路步行街與各大百貨；若想住小資翻新平價高 CP 值，則推薦步行可達南京東路站的「上海南京路假日酒店」，房內更附設免費洗烘衣機。
Q2：想在房間躺著看東方明珠與黃浦江「一線無敵夜景」，最推薦預訂哪幾間飯店？
A：浦西外灘首推極致服務的「上海半岛酒店（上海半島酒店）」 與前衛潮流的「上海外滩Ｗ酒店（上海外灘W酒店）」，大片落地窗直面陸家嘴天際線；浦東陸家嘴則首推「上海浦东丽思卡尔顿酒店（上海浦東麗思卡爾頓酒店）」，客房與頂樓 Flair Bar 平視東方明珠塔身，震撼感無與倫比。
Q3：專程帶小孩去玩「上海迪士尼樂園」，住園區哪間官方飯店最省心、CP 值最高？
A：追求高 CP 值首推「玩具總動員酒店」！享有官方提前入園特權，清晨專屬穿梭巴士免排長隊，房內滿滿巴斯光年元素且提供語音叫醒服務；若追求頂級度假感與角色互動，則推薦「上海迪士尼樂園酒店」，早餐有米奇米妮親自桌邊合照，還能搭乘星願湖專屬客船優雅入園。
上海住宿總結
來上海玩，不知道住哪的話，選對區域真的很重要！如果想看夜景、享受奢華氛圍，住外灘附近準沒錯，像是半島、W、文華東方這類上海五星飯店，房間舒適、景觀絕美，服務也超貼心；要逛街吃美食，南京路或人民廣場一帶超方便，交通四通八達，像上海康萊德酒店、上海艾迪遜酒店都很不錯。親子旅遊的話，浦東迪士尼周邊也有不少高CP值飯店。不管你是想拍美照、耍廢放鬆還是走路玩景點，上海都有對應的住宿選擇可以滿足！

title: 【上海城隍廟+豫園遊玩攻略】含到達交通、遊玩路線、美食和購物等 - Go Travelling World
text:
2026-09-11 晚風輕輕吹上海旅遊城隍廟, 豫園0 Comments 
上海城隍廟和豫園毗鄰，相距不超過百米，因此很多遊客都是把這兩個景點放在一起遊玩。
此外，城隍廟和豫園之間還有一個豫園商城，這裏不僅是一個大型購物美食商圈，而且建築大都是仿古建築，夜晚開燈會非常好看，是上海最美夜景地之一。當然不能錯過的還有外灘那邊的美景了，可以看【上海外灘一日遊】最佳遊玩路線順序推薦。
因此本篇攻略會把城隍廟、豫園、豫園商城都一起做了，希望能幫助大家更好地遊玩這裏。
延伸閱讀：【上海自由行】三天兩晚自由行全攻略，交通、行程、住宿、美食

上海豫園城隍廟遊玩常見Q&A
上海豫園城隍廟交通攻略
1、地鐵：上海市內乘坐地鐵10號線或14號線，在豫園站下車，1號出口出。(推薦搭乘地鐵，快速方便)
✅️地鐵巴士卡購買：中國大陸巴士地鐵一卡通
2、公交：
乘坐932路到城隍廟站下車;
乘坐64路、715路在複興東路光啟路站下車;
乘坐24路、581路到豫園站下車;
乘坐11路(內圈、外圈)、64路、304路夜班空調、736路、736路空調、801路、920路、926路空調、930路在新北門站下車。
乘坐11路(內圈、外圈)、64路、304路夜班空調在人民路新開河路站下車。
上海豫園城隍廟遊玩路線
上海豫園城隍廟片區遊玩路線推薦：
豫園地鐵站1號口→福佑小商品市場→童涵春堂中藥博物館→大壺春(豫園店)→豫園南門(大門)→豫園西門→九曲橋和湖心亭→挹秀樓→南翔饅頭館或綠波廊午餐→巧克力博物館→海上梨園→城隍廟→豫園商城
上海城隍廟豫園遊玩路線圖
上海豫園城隍廟遊玩景點
福佑小商品市場
豫園地鐵站1號口旁邊就是福佑小商品市場，裏面商品都可以還價，建議臉皮厚一點，不還價會虧。可以先逛逛挑選一些紀念品帶回家。
童涵春堂中藥博物館
這家百年中草藥店門口掛滿了各種香囊，不同節氣有不同的寓意!博物館位於4樓，免費開放。
大壺春(豫園店)
大壺春是上海老字號品牌，尤其以生煎包最為有名，如果是早上過來的可以來這邊吃個早餐。營業時間09:00-22:00。
豫園
豫園是一個園林景點，園內古色古香，適合拍照，每一處景致都獨特。遊玩時長大約是2小時。
上海豫園導覽圖
豫園遊玩路線推薦：
豫園南門→三穗堂→仰山堂→大假山→魚樂榭→萃秀堂→亦舫→複廊→學圃→點春堂→快樓→九獅軒→和煦堂→老君殿→會景樓→流觴亭→玉華堂→藏書樓→玉玲瓏→環龍橋→涵碧樓→內園→靜觀→洞天福地→聳翠亭→可以觀→還雲樓→古戲台→豫園西門
豫园始建于明嘉靖三十八年(1559年) ，距今已有460多年历史。主人潘允端是四川布政使，为了让辞官告老的父亲安享晚年，在祖宅西侧修建了这座园林。“豫”字取自《易经》，寓意“平安”“安泰”，也藏着“愉悦老亲”的一片孝心。
如今的豫园占地近30亩(约2万平方米) ，分为三穗堂、万花楼、点春堂、会景楼、玉华堂、内园六大景区。园内亭台楼阁、假山池水、龙墙花廊层层叠叠，被誉为 “虽由人作，宛自天开” 。#上海豫园旅游攻略
大假山(豫园精华之最)
由明代造园名家张南阳亲自设计堆叠，用2000吨武康石堆砌而成，高约14米。层峦叠嶂如真山，是江南现存明代黄石假山之最巨者——登顶可俯瞰整座园林。
玉玲珑(镇园之宝)
江南三大名石之一。相传是宋徽宗“花石纲”的遗物——就是《水浒传》里“智取生辰纲”那个“花石纲”。高约3米，石上72个孔洞，呈现“百孔淌泉，百孔冒烟”的奇观。古人说它“一炉香置孔中，则众孔皆烟”，站在石前，你会明白什么叫“皱、漏、瘦、透”。
三穗堂
堂高9米，五开间，华丽宽敞。抬头看“三穗堂”“灵台经始”“城市山林”三块贴金匾额——“城市山林”正是园主的心愿：身居闹市，却拥有山林野趣。
内园
原为城隍庙庙园，建于1709年，占地仅2亩。虽小，却有“螺蛳壳里做道场”的精妙。
豫園營業時間：9:00-16:30，16:00停止入場，周一休息。門票旺季40元，淡季30元。
豫園參觀信息：https://www.yugarden.com.cn/page/articleView/message.html
✅️門票預訂：Klook
九曲橋
豫園西門出來就可以看到九曲橋和湖心亭，不妨去走走，步步有轉，五步有彎，可以去除黴運，好運相隨。湖面上還會不定期舉辦各種主題的燈會展示。
九曲橋
挹秀樓
挹秀樓坐落在豫園商城中心，九曲橋旁邊，是一座西方歐洲風格的青磚木結構洋樓。樓內設有上下兩層回廊，建築風格別具一格，古樸典雅。
挹秀樓有著悠久的建造曆史，後經修繕成為永安抗戰文化名人館，館內展示著各類英雄事跡。
南翔饅頭店或綠波廊(午餐)
南翔饅頭店和綠波廊都是上海有名的老字號，南翔饅頭店主打小籠包和蟹黃灌湯包。
綠波廊則是國宴級別的酒樓，代表菜式有八寶鴨、糯米鴨、灌湯包、蟹粉包等。
巧克力博物館
位於舊校場路69號2-3樓。展館展示了用巧克力制成的動物展區，彌漫著濃鬱的巧克力香味，還有用巧克力制成的包包、鞋子、花瓶等。可以參觀免費，結束後還可品嘗小巧克力豆。
海上梨園
原是俯瞰豫園的一處戲台，如今已經發展成近千平方米的空中庭院。浸入式舞台呈現的傳統建築與餐飲區域完美融合，營造出優雅賞樂的奇妙氛圍。這裏會不定期舉行演出，需購票入場。
城隍廟
上海城隍廟是上海道教正一派的主要道觀之一，景點免費，不過要繳10元進香費。
城隍廟官網：https://shchm.org/shchm/
上海城隍廟導覽圖
上海城隍廟，原為金山廟(又名霍光行祠)，供奉西漢大將軍博陸侯霍光。上海城隍廟始建於明代永樂年間(1403年-1424年)，供奉敕封上海城隍神秦裕伯，是道教正一派的宮觀。
上海城隍廟供奉的城隍神為【秦裕伯】，元代進士，因道德高尚、仗義執言，被民眾尊崇。雖曾拒絕朱元璋的招攬，但後為國請命而入朝為官。羽化後，朱元璋贊其生不為臣、死當衛土，民眾遂奉其為上海城隍神，期望其守護上海安寧。
地址：上海市黃浦區方浜中路249號
交通：【地鐵10號線、14號線】豫園地鐵站7號口
門票：10元(可領三只清香)
開放時間：5月1日——9月30日，開放時間為9:00-17:00;
10月1日——來年4月30日，開放時間為8:30-16:30。(逢農曆初一、十五，本廟開放時間為清晨6:00起，如遇春節等特殊時段，開放時間以公告為准。)
城隍廟方位布局
城隍廟殿堂建築屬南方大式建築，但在建築風格上仍保持著明代格局。
整前後共三進：第一進供的是霍光;第二進供的是秦裕伯;第三進是城隍夫人。
建築沿中軸線依次排列，廟內主體建築有大殿、元辰殿、父母殿等十二個殿堂，樓下西側由南而北為三官殿、財神殿、客堂;東側由南而北為月老殿、慈航殿祈福堂。儀門對面中軸線上為霍光殿，背後連接一條通向後院的長廊，名為太歲殿。出太歲殿，即為後院，正面為城隍殿，西側為關聖殿，東側為文昌殿。
上海城隍廟各殿介紹
上海城隍廟主要殿宇有三官殿、月老殿、財神殿、慈航殿、祈福堂、霍光殿、元辰殿、關帝殿、文昌殿、城隍殿、娘娘殿、育德殿等。遊玩的時候按照建築布局從南到北遊玩即可。
山門照壁
在明朝嘉靖十四年(1535年)建造的，已有四百五十年以上的曆史。上面有四個金色大字“保障海隅”，原來是由明代上海縣知縣馮彬題寫的。
儀門
儀門是過去官衙的第二道正門，儀門前面有二副對聯。對聯的後面掛著一只很大的算盤，上刻著四個字“不由人算”。
城隍廟大殿
大殿內供奉金山神主漢代博陸侯霍光大將軍坐像，左首為文判官，右首為武判官，次為日巡與夜查，日巡、夜查以下為八皂隸。
太歲殿
又稱元辰殿、六十甲子殿。元，為“善”，元辰，就是指吉利時日的意思。因六十甲子神靈是星神，故也稱太歲神。
三官殿
三官殿中供奉的是主管【天上事務】、【地上事務】和【水中事務】的神靈，號天官、地官和水官。
月老殿
供奉月老【主姻緣】、藥王爺孫思邈【主身體健康】、車神【主路途平安】。
慈航殿
供奉眼母娘娘【主治眼疾】、慈航大士【主平安】、天後娘娘【主出海平安】。
財神殿
殿內供奉有五位財神。中間是趙公明，左面和右面是他的部下招寶天尊蕭昇和納珍天尊曹寶。在財神殿兩邊的是招財使者陳九公和利市仙官姚少司。
城隍殿
供奉的就是明代敕封的上海縣城隍【秦裕伯】，城隍殿西面為娘娘殿，供奉上海縣城隍神夫人儲氏。城隍殿東首為父母殿，殿內供奉上海縣城隍神父母。
文昌殿
文昌帝君，即梓潼帝君主管人的【功名和祿位】
關聖殿
上海城隍廟的天井左邊是關帝殿。供關聖帝君，左右供周倉、關平二位將軍，其中關帝具有【管理命祿】、【保佑科舉】等職能。
豫園商城
這裏吃喝玩樂樣樣俱全，等到晚上燈光亮起時更是美不勝收。在這裏，你可以看到古老的弄堂和高樓並存的景象，展現了上海的迷人魅力。

2026上海豫園燈會
2026上海豫園燈會“來大豫園過上海年”於1月26日璀璨亮燈，拉開上海年味的帷幕。豫園民俗藝術燈區將率先點亮，由此開啟一場36天的海派年味之旅。(豫園民俗藝術燈區2月16日除夕不亮燈)。
本次豫園民俗藝術燈區實行分時段憑票入場，高峰日(每周五至周日、農曆初一至初七、元宵節)14:00-22:00入場，普通日16:00-22:00入場，成人票80元，兒童票、軍人票、老年人票50元，詳見↓
今年，豫園燈會首次延伸至古城公園、方浜中路、福佑路、外灘，並通過精心設計的馬年主題燈組，巧妙地連接起BFC外灘金融中心，呈現“六區一體”的新格局。以“回家過年”為敘事主線，串聯一條由豫園到BFC再到外灘的“曆史—現代—未來”光影敘事帶，全方位打造充滿溫情、煙火氣與儀式感的“上海過年必到路線”。
在這裏，可以重溫老上海的濃鬱年味，品上海味道、逛新春市集、賞文化演繹、享科技互動、買文創年貨、購上海禮物。讓老上海人找回記憶，讓新上海人理解傳統，讓遊客體驗海派春節。市民遊客、海外賓朋都可以來到大豫園，共同體驗上海地道年味。
豫園BFC外灘以光影合體新格局，一票通玩六個燈區!
本屆燈會從單一的豫園民俗藝術燈區，擴展至覆蓋大豫園片區的六大主題燈區，形成一條從豫園延伸至BFC外灘的連貫觀燈動線。
豫園民俗藝術燈區延續文化主題
其中，市民朋友最為熟悉的豫園民俗藝術燈區推出“山海奇豫記”第四季《曠野篇》(分時段憑票入場)，將於1月26日率先點亮，以非遺燈彩技藝，融合數智光影藝術，呈現一場文化與科技的視覺盛宴。“以夢為馬，曠野生花”的主題，表達人生是“曠野”而非“軌道”，鼓勵人們在變化無常的世界中，如駿馬般踏實努力，在山海間勇敢逐夢，把內心夢想變成美好現實。
從滿載祥瑞的“福祿之門”步入璀璨燈海之中，一幅幅喜慶的楹聯承載著滿滿的年味與祝福，率先映入眼簾，與黃金廣場的巨型走馬燈相映成趣;走馬燈內玲瓏剔透的鏤空雕花與燈光交融，呈現一派“葫光流轉，萬象呈祥”的意境。漫步凝暉路，“舞馬踏福”燈組淩空飛馳，以三段不同主題詮釋三重人生意境。
轉入中心廣場，“駿馳九州，步步生花”的六匹駿馬，仿佛踏破時空，昂首飛馳在天地山海之間。一側的銀杏樹下“事事如意”燈組蘊藏著“如意繁榮”的美好寓意，為每一位遊客送上新春祝福。文昌街，融彙了從敦煌、洛陽博物館代表性館藏珍品中提取的元素，帶著吉祥如意裝點新春。
“馬躍星河，逐夢蒼穹”的場景在九曲橋緩緩展開，湖面化為星海，二十八星宿列布，現實與傳說於此交織，形成一場可步入、可觸摸的東方生活美學體驗。此外，晏海閣“馬踏飛花”、五號門“一路繁花”，與舊校場路年味市集相連，遊人可邊賞燈邊挑選新春年貨、品嘗美食風味、購買上海禮物，在光影交織中沉浸於濃鬱的節慶氛圍。
今年豫園還與小布聯名推出特別企劃。可愛的“兔小布”化身夢想播報員，悄悄藏進四個核心燈組中——黃金廣場、凝暉路、中心廣場、九曲橋。遊客在遊覽中尋找隱藏的兔小布，更有驚喜等待著大家，讓我們一起尋夢豫園，“布布”生花。
五大免費燈區特色鮮明
今年，BFC首次以風尚潮流燈區煥彩開場，全周期免費開放。BFC聯合泡泡瑪特傾情打造新春遊園會，可愛的IP們一齊換上馬年點金奔騰新裝扮，彙聚在外灘送上新春祝福，各式祈福燈組也帶來沉浸式潮玩互動體驗，更有新春點金奔騰主題快閃店呈現獨家好禮。
BFC的新春玩樂不僅於此：拍洋畫、跳房子、懷舊街機等年味體驗彙聚南區B2複古街區;外灘楓徑裝飾靈動馬燈，一系列年味市集繽紛開啟，帶來時髦年俗好禮。上海複星藝術中心以“紋”以載道——故宮博物院沉浸式數字體驗展開年，詮釋東方美學底蘊。這個春節，BFC風尚潮流燈區將打造既熟悉又充滿新意的潮流中國年，為魔都帶來五光十色的過年新樂趣。
此外，四個燈區同時免費開放，福佑路燈區以“流光巷陌，煙火福佑”營造溫暖街巷;方浜中路燈區以“萬家燈火，方浜往事”回溯上海記憶;古城公園燈區則以“闔家團圓，古城年味”洋溢團圓氣息;外灘燈區以“璀璨江岸，外灘華章”展現現代風華。四重主題交織呼應，既傳遞上海的親切年味，又閃耀時尚潮流的繽紛光彩，在點亮城市的同時，也自然而然地引領遊客步入豫園、BFC和外灘，體驗完整而層次豐富的觀燈之旅。五個免費燈區也將陸續點亮，2月1日將實現六區同亮。
上海豫園城隍廟附近美食
首先說明一下，上海豫園城隍廟片區作為旅遊熱門區域，這裏的美食小吃在整個上海來說價格也是偏貴的，所以不太建議特地來這邊吃上海美食。
不過如果來豫園和城隍廟遊玩，可以順便吃一下這邊的美食，這裏的上海特色美食還是很豐富的，老字號比較多，以下是一些推薦：
大壺春
大壺春是上海著名老字號生煎品牌，這裏的生煎以皮厚、湯汁少為特點，面皮酥脆口感紮實，配上點米醋可以解除油膩感，再搭配一碗咖喱牛肉粉絲湯就是完美的早餐搭配。
南翔饅頭店
始建於1900年，至今仍是上海品嘗小籠包的熱門去處。如果不想排隊，可以選擇外賣打包，方便外帶和品嘗。
南翔饅頭店主打鮮肉小籠包湯汁豐盈，肉質鮮嫩，42元一屜，一共6個。
豫園城隍廟美食店家分布
綠波廊
這家餐廳可是國宴級別的酒樓。特別是他們的糯米鴨，簡直是一絕，但要注意每日供應量有限。這裏的點心也好吃，有蟹黃灌湯包、蛋黃酥、玫瑰餅、青餅等。
松月樓
有百年曆史，特色淨素菜包年銷售400萬只，味道經典，馬蘭頭松子青團也很值得嘗試，美味可口。
寧波湯圓
他們的湯圓個頭大，外皮軟糯，內餡鮮美，尤其是芝麻口味。
沈大成
主打各種糕點和青團。他們家的鹹蛋黃肉松青團美味無比，肉松的鮮味和鴨蛋黃的鹹香相得益彰，是絕妙的搭配。
光明冷飲
光明是上海人民鍾愛的牛奶品牌。在將上世紀的經典光明冰磚變成飲品後，口感更加濃鬱絲滑。底部的珍珠和咖啡液則更迎合年輕人的口味。
童涵春堂
供應古方茶飲，茶品種類豐富，都是養生配方，可以在店內用餐或外帶。
城隍廟素齋
在城隍廟內(就是寺廟裏)，面條僅售20塊一碗，澆頭15塊一個，種類繁多。素菜包、蝴蝶酥、雲片糕都非常美味，值得推薦的還有大餛飩!
除了城隍廟內，城隍廟外的舊校場路開設了一條美食街，這裏有很多上海特色美食，比如臭豆腐，都能在這裏找到。
上海豫園城隍廟購物推薦
老城隍廟食品商店
上海特產推薦來這家商店，奶糖、牛軋糖、五香豆等等都可以買得到，比較推薦購買上海梨膏糖、大白兔奶糖等。
舊校場路
這條街除了有各種美食小吃之外，還有各種上海特產可以購買。
上海住宿推薦：【上海住宿酒店】上海必住的七家酒店性價比
上海豫園城隍廟遊玩常見Q&A
重要區分：豫園(明代古典園林，收費)≠豫園商城 / 老街 / 九曲橋(免費商圈);城隍廟是獨立道觀，單獨售票，很多遊客容易混淆。
Q：上海豫園值得去嗎?
值得去：想看江南古典園林、古建築、中式美學，喜歡漢服拍照、了解上海老城廂曆史，推薦進豫園園林;只打卡紅燈籠老街、九曲橋夜景、吃小吃，免費街區就足夠，氛圍感很強。
Q：豫園要買門票嗎?
豫園商城、九曲橋、豫園老街全天免費，不用門票攜程。
豫園園林(裏面的江南古園)：旺季(4.1–6.30、9.1–11.30)40 元;淡季(7.1–8.31、12.1–次年 3.31)30 元;周一常規閉園(法定節假日除外)，16:00 停止入園攜程。
城隍廟道觀：香花券 10 元，入園贈送 3 支清香，不要在外面小販手裏高價買香攜程。
優待：全日制學生、60–69 周歲老人園林門票半價;1.3 米以下兒童、70 周歲以上老人、現役軍人、殘疾人憑證免園林門票。
Q：上海豫園要逛多久?
只逛豫園園林內部：1.5 小時左右
園林 + 城隍廟道觀：2.5–3 小時
園林 + 城隍廟 + 九曲橋 + 豫園老街(含夜景)：半天(3–4 小時)
僅免費街區(九曲橋 + 老街打卡拍照吃小吃)：1–2 小時
Q：豫園裏面有什麼?
豫園園林(收費)：明代江南古典園林，核心看點：玉玲瓏(鎮園之寶，江南三大奇石)、大假山(明代黃石假山)、三穗堂、點春堂、萬花樓、龍牆、內園古戲台，亭台樓閣、池塘假山，一步一景，屬於全國文保單位攜程。
豫園商城 / 外圍免費區域：九曲橋、湖心亭茶樓、紅燈籠老街、老字號商鋪、小吃店、文創店;可以看夜景。
Q：上海城隍廟靈驗嗎?
祈福屬於傳統文化心理寄托，心誠則靈，沒有客觀層面 “靈驗與否” 的科學說法。城隍廟是上海知名的道教正一派道觀，有 600 多年曆史，上海本地人和遊客常來祈福，求平安、事業、姻緣等，更多是一種心願寄托。
Q：上海城隍廟拜什麼?
主殿供奉上海城隍秦裕伯(城市保護神)，大殿先拜城隍;各殿分管不同祈願：
財神殿：五路財神，求財運、事業順遂
月老殿：求姻緣、良緣
三官殿：三官大帝，消災解難、祈求順遂
太歲殿：拜太歲，適合本命年
慈航殿：慈航、媽祖、眼光娘娘，可求平安、護佑家人等
 城隍廟, 豫園 
 Written by 晚風輕輕吹

11天中国经典之旅：北京、西安、桂林和上海 
这条精心设计的11天中国经典之旅，将带您全面舒适地领略中国风情。从漫步北京长城、探寻故宫的神秘，到乘船游览漓江，欣赏壮丽的石灰岩山峰，再到感受现代上海的活力，这段旅程将历史、文化、自然和都市生活完美融合，为您打造一段难忘的中国之旅。 
 定制此行程
 11 Days / 10 Nights 
 中国经典影片精华片段，节奏把握得当。 
 北京 → 西安 → 桂林 → 上海 
 最受欢迎的中国经典路线。 
 私人旅游体验 
 私人导游、司机，行程安排灵活。 
 非常适合初次到访者 
 中国入门指南。 
主页 / 十大旅游线路 / 11天中国经典之旅：北京、西安、桂林和上海
这段旅程有何不同之处 
 一家在香港注册的旅行社 
 由香港集团支持，在中国各地设有本地团队。 
 安全付款 
 可使用 Visa、MasterCard、Apple Pay、PayPal 或银行转账安全支付。 
 24/7客服支持 
 在您前往中国之前、期间和之后，我们将为您提供真正的人工帮助。 
 定制体验 
 根据您的兴趣和旅行方式量身定制活动和行程节奏。 
推荐的11天中国经典行程 
 天目的地体验焦点
 第 1-4 天中国长城漫步、故宫、天坛、静谧颐和园
 第 5-6 天西安兵马俑、古城墙、穆斯林街区及当地文化
 第 7-9 天桂林、阳朔漓江游船之旅，欣赏石灰岩山峰和乡村风光
 第 10-11 天上海外滩、上海中心大厦天际线、新旧城市对比
这段旅程是如何无缝衔接的 
这条精心设计的路线连接了中国西南地区最具标志性的自然景点，将成都、九寨沟、黄龙和张家界连接起来，使旅程流畅而节奏适宜。
为了确保旅途舒适高效，我们采用高速列车短途出行，国内航班长途出行，并根据需要提供私人接送服务。这种平衡的出行方式最大限度地减少了旅途时间，同时最大限度地增加了您亲近自然的时间，让您能够以轻松的节奏旅行，悠闲地享受每个目的地。 
国内长途航班
高速列车用于短途线路 
这条为期11天的中国经典之旅有何不同之处 
这条为期11天的中国经典之旅专为那些想要体验更深度文化之旅的旅行者而设计。每一项体验都经过精心挑选，旨在提供更深入的文化洞察、更顺畅的旅程以及更真实的中国体验。 
揭开中国皇宫不为人知的故事
探索紫禁城较为安静的殿堂，通过讲故事的方式了解皇帝、妃嫔和朝廷官员的真实生活，这是普通观光旅游中很少见到的。 
领略长城的不同风貌 
漫步慕田峪长城风景优美的一段，感受其恢弘的气势和精湛的工程技艺。部分行程还包含欣赏司马台长城迷人的夜景。 
品尝正宗北京美食 
在当地知名餐厅品尝正宗北京烤鸭，体验超越旅游菜单的城市饮食文化。 
超越第一印象 
参观兵马俑，在专业导游的带领下，深入了解秦始皇的军队、工艺和古代军事体系。 
乘船游览中国最具标志性的风景 
在漓江上乘坐游船放松身心，欣赏壮丽的石灰岩山峰、河畔村庄以及20元人民币纸币上描绘的风景。 
从外滩的历史故事到天际线景观 
漫步于历史悠久的外滩，聆听上海黄金时代的故事，然后登上上海中心大厦，俯瞰现代中国的全景。 
真实旅行者时刻 
快速了解一下这次私人旅行的体验——从北京到上海，真实的旅行者照片、当地风情和正宗的中国美食。 
详细的11天中国经典行程安排 
以下是建议的每日行程安排。所有细节均可根据您的兴趣、旅行节奏和时间安排进行调整。 
 第一天——抵达北京 | 中国之旅顺利开启 
欢迎来到中国首都北京。
抵达北京首都国际机场后，您的私人导游将在到达大厅迎接您，并乘坐舒适的私人车辆护送您前往酒店。
您的导游将协助您搬运行李和办理酒店入住，确保您轻松抵达。当天剩余时间您可以自由休息或在附近散步，以便从旅途疲劳中恢复过来，并调整到当地时间。
为什么选择这一天很合适：
✔ 没有观光压力
✔ 是时候休息和适应了
✔ 自抵达之日起提供个人协助 
 第二天——北京精华游 | 天坛与故宫 
早餐午餐
清晨，您可以从天坛开始您的一天，这里曾是历代皇帝祈求五谷丰登的地方。您还会看到当地居民练习太极拳、跳舞和其他传统运动，让您一窥北京的日常生活。
在一家颇受欢迎的当地餐厅享用正宗中式午餐后，步行穿过天安门广场，进入故宫——世界上规模最大、保存最完好的皇家宫殿。您的导游不会带您走人潮拥挤的路线，而是会带领您游览较为安静的区域，并为您讲述皇室生活、宫廷礼仪以及明清两代的历史故事。
可选定制：
胡同人力车之旅
当地市场考察
在当地家庭制作饺子
导游会根据您的兴趣调整行程节奏和重点。 
 第三天——长城体验 | 风景漫步与标志性景观 
早餐后，驱车前往慕田峪长城，这里以秀丽的景色和保存完好的古道而闻名。在导游的带领下，您可以悠闲地漫步长城，细细品味其雄伟的规模、精湛的工程技艺以及周围壮丽的山景。
对于想要体验特别之旅的旅客，部分行程可能包括下午参观司马台长城，您可以欣赏到夜晚灯光璀璨的长城——与白天的参观视角截然不同。
这一天为何如此特别：
✔ 均衡的步行时间
✔ 风景优美、人流较少的路段
✔ 可选择体验夜间活动，无需承担任何义务
餐食： 早餐+午餐
个性化提示：
想轻松游览？那就选择慕田峪，乘坐往返缆车吧。
想要更惊艳的体验？那就添加司马台夜景（季节性）吧！ 
 第四天——颐和园和西安高铁 
早餐午餐
早餐后，返回北京参观颐和园，这座中国园林艺术的杰作，是昔日皇室休闲生活的完美典范。漫步于静谧的湖泊、典雅的走廊和幽静的花园，感受昔日帝王和皇室成员的休憩之所。
下午，前往火车站，搭乘高铁前往西安。这段高效的铁路旅程让您能够舒适地穿梭于中国各大城市之间，同时体验中国现代化的基础设施。
抵达后，当地导游将迎接您并护送您前往位于市中心的酒店。
为什么选择这一天很合适：
✔ 均衡游览，不赶时间
✔ 北京和西安之间的平稳过渡
✔ 乘坐高速列车享受舒适的旅程 
 第五天——兵马俑和古城墙 
早餐午餐
今天，你将探索世界上最重要的考古发现之一——兵马俑。
参观博物馆群，欣赏为守护秦始皇陵而建造的庞大地下军队。导游将为您讲解这些兵马俑的制作、排列和保存方式，帮助您了解它们在中国古代历史上的重要意义。
下午，参观西安古城墙，它是中国保存最完好的城墙之一。您可以沿着城墙漫步或​​骑行，欣赏西安内城的全景，感受古代遗迹与现代生活交相辉映的景象。
体验亮点：
✔ 兵马俑及专家讲解
✔ 古城墙漫步或​​骑行
✔ 深入了解中国帝国军事史 
 第六天——西安市区观光及飞往桂林 
早餐午餐
今天的行程从陕西历史博物馆开始，馆内展出数千件文物，展现了中国文明历代发展历程。之后前往大雁塔，这座地标性建筑与佛教在中国的传播密切相关。
随后，您将游览热闹的回民街，这里以熙熙攘攘的氛围、传统小吃和充满活力的当地文化而闻名。导游将为您介绍当地特色美食，并讲解不同社群如何塑造了西安的历史。
下午，前往机场搭乘国内航班前往桂林，欣赏中国著名的山水风光。
为什么旅行者喜欢这一天：
✔ 对西安历史重要性的清晰概述
✔ 地道的当地市场氛围
✔ 与中国南方交通便捷 
 第七天——龙脊梯田与少数民族文化 
早餐午餐
早餐后，驱车前往龙脊梯田，这里是中国最令人叹为观止的农业景观之一。龙脊梯田依山而建，历经数百年，随着季节变换色彩——春天水波荡漾，秋收时节金黄灿烂。
漫步于层层叠叠的梯田之间，从观景台俯瞰山谷全景。了解当地壮族和瑶族少数民族如何适应山区生活，并保留了传统的木屋、耕作方式和习俗。
与当地家庭共进午餐，体验当地文化，例如制作竹筒饭和品尝新鲜制作的油茶。此次行程让您有机会深入了解远离中国大城市的乡村生活。
这一天为何如此特别：
✔ 壮观的梯田景色
✔ 体验地道的少数族裔文化
✔ 步行速度适中，沿途风景优美 
 第 8 天 — 漓江游船 |桂林飞往阳朔 
早餐午餐
今天我们将体验中国旅游中最具标志性的体验之一——漓江游船之旅。
悠闲地乘船游览，欣赏江水蜿蜒流经壮丽的石灰岩山峰、竹林和宁静的村庄。沿途，您或许会看到农民在稻田里劳作，水牛在河中嬉戏，构成一幅幅如诗如画的画面，展现了桂林的自然之美。
午后早些时候在阳朔下船，您可以游览以热闹氛围和特色小店而闻名的西街。之后前往位于郊区的酒店，享受悠闲时光。
阳朔可选活动：
烹饪课
太极拳课程
骑自行车穿过乡村 
 第9天——乡村生活及飞往上海 
早餐午餐
上午可以探索阳朔乡村，穿梭于宁静的村庄和乡间小路。这里与中国的大城市形成鲜明对比，展现了日常生活的另一面。
参观当地集市，了解村民如何购买日常必需品。导游会讲解当地的食材和习俗，帮助您更好地了解乡村传统和价值观。
下午，前往机场搭乘国内航班飞往中国最具活力的现代化城市上海。
为什么旅行者喜欢这一天：
✔ 地道的乡村生活体验
✔ 深入了解当地农民的日常生活
✔ 从自然到现代中国的平稳过渡 
 第十天——上海精华游 | 古老与现代的中国 
早餐午餐
抵达上海，中国最具国际化和活力的现代化都市。今天，您将探索上海古今交融的迷人景象，殖民历史、传统文化与未来主义的摩天大楼在此和谐共存。
从上海标志性的外滩开始您的旅程。漫步于始建于20世纪初的历史建筑之间，了解上海如何发展成为全球贸易中心。您的导游将分享一些鲜为人知的故事，揭示这座城市不为人知的过去。
继续前往法租界，这里以绿树成荫的街道、欧式建筑和轻松的氛围而闻名。这片区域让您得以一窥上海的历史街区和日常生活。
午餐后，登上中国最高的建筑——上海中心大厦。从观景台上，您可以饱览城市天际线的全景——与下方历史悠久的外滩形成鲜明的视觉对比。
晚上，您可以选择乘坐黄浦江游船，或者放松身心，悠闲地欣赏上海迷人的夜景。

✔ 步行和观光节奏均衡
